The lawmakers expressed serious concern over the alleged arrests and undisclosed whereabouts of Afridi, Swati, Junaid Akbar Khan, MNAs Dr Amjad, Fazal Muhammad Khan, Naseem Shah, Iqbal Afridi and Zubair Wazir, along with provincial ministers and MPAs.

They demanded that all detained elected representatives be immediately brought before the public and produced before the relevant courts.

“Their families should be informed about the reasons for their arrests and places of detention, while they must be granted the full legal right to defend themselves,” the statement said.

The PTI members stressed that depriving elected representatives of their political activities and keeping them in undisclosed detention amounted to an assault on democratic values and the public mandate.

In last month’s comments on detentions after governor’s rule, Minister of State for Interior Tallal Chaudhry had said those with cases against them will be tried, while others would be released.

The participants also condemned the recent detentions of former provincial minister Taimur Saleem Jhagra, Kamran Bangash and Irfan Saleem under the MPO, asserting that their arrests despite protective bail granted by the Peshawar High Court raised serious questions about respect for judicial orders and the rule of law.

The PTI lawmakers demanded that the three leaders be immediately produced before the court, released and provided with all legal facilities, the statement said.

Former National Assembly speaker Asad Qaiser, along with MNAs Atif Khan, Saleem Rehman, Sahibzada Sibghatullah, Mehboob Shah, Shahram Khan Tarakai, Shahzada Gastasap, Muhammad Nawaz Khan, Asif Khan, Ali Asghar Khan, Arbab Sher Ali, Sohail Sultan, Ali Khan Jadoon, Sajid Momand, Shah Ahad and Bashir Khan, attended the meeting.

The PTI statement comes a day after it emerged that President Asif Ali Zardari promulgated an ordinance, doing away with most of the “privileges” of KP lawmakers, including protection against “preventive detention”.

Through an amendment ordinance related to the privileges of MPAs, drastic changes have been made in the KP Provincial Assembly (Powers, Immunities and Privileges) Act 2026, as 21 of its 40 sections have been omitted, including those providing protection to the MPAs against “preventive detentions” and offences related to “breach” of privileges.

Four other ordinances promulgated provided a legal framework for special initiatives in the designated 12 districts and other districts in the province.

With the imposition of emergency in KP on Oct 11, an Area Representative and Development Council (ARDC) was formed to oversee 12 districts that were deemed to face intense security challenges, including the merged districts.

On governor’s rule and ongoing political situation

The meeting also condemned reported raids on the homes of PTI workers and detentions under MPO following the imposition of governor’s rule in KP on Oct 11.

The participants alleged harassment of political workers, violation of the sanctity of homes and restrictions on political activities, condemning them as “blatant violations of the Constitution and fundamental human rights”. They demanded the immediate release of all detained party workers.

Rejecting the imposition of governor’s rule in KP on the pretext of terrorism, the meeting asserted that the PTI provincial government had consistently adopted a zero-tolerance policy against terrorism. The participants said terrorism could not be “used as a political tool to undermine the democratic mandate” of the province.

They called for the immediate and effective implementation of the National Action Plan and strict adherence to a resolution adopted by all political parties in KP.

During the meeting, PTI leaders claimed that governor’s rule had further aggravated the province’s political, economic and administrative challenges. It also criticised KP Governor Kundi, saying that instead of representing the federation and playing a constructive role in resolving provincial issues, his actions were further complicating the situation.

The participants expressed “serious concern” over delays by the federal government in releasing KP’s financial entitlements and deductions from its resources. They said Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif had promised Rs160 billion to the province, but under a new agreement, the federal government had made deductions of approximately Rs157bn, which they termed an injustice to the people of the province.

According to the statement, they contended that the federal government was “treating the province like a stepchild” under the pretext of governor’s rule and stressed that the people of the province could not be deprived of their constitutional and financial rights.

The meeting also expressed concern over the withdrawal of security provided to JUI-F chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman. The participants maintained that ensuring the security of all political leaders, irrespective of political differences, was the responsibility of the state. They demanded that Fazl and other leaders of his party be immediately provided with the required security.

The participants welcomed PPP scion Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari’s statement describing Imran as a political prisoner and his support for PTI’s position on the reserved seats issue. They termed Imran a major political stakeholder and said that attempts to exclude him from the political process were detrimental to democracy.

They stressed that the PPP should go beyond statements and take practical steps, calling for Bilawal to dissociate himself from the imposition of governor’s rule and not vote for its extension in the NA.

The meeting concluded with a “reaffirmation of the participants’ commitment to the supremacy of the Constitution and the rule of law, the protection of political freedoms, safeguarding the province’s constitutional and financial rights, respect for the public mandate and ensuring the security of all political leaders”, the statement added.

PTI seeks Imran’s access to personal physician

According to the statement, the meeting also discussed in detail the health and treatment of incarcerated PTI founder Imran Khan, the law and order situation in KP, concerns over the imposition of governor’s rule, the province’s constitutional and financial rights, and the overall political situation in the country.

Imran has been in prison since Aug 5, 2023, while his wife was arrested on Jan 17, 2025 in a separate case in which the couple were sentenced. The IHC has allowed him twice-a-week meetings with his family, lawyers and other associates, but despite multiple court directives, the meetings have been largely restricted.

Imran and Bushra’s lawyers were able to meet the couple earlier this month after a gap of several months, after the Islamabad High Court issued directives for the meeting to aid legal consultation.

In the meeting, PTI lawmakers demanded that all facilities be provided to Imran in accordance with the jail manual and Supreme Court (SC) judgments.

They called for him to have immediate access to his personal physician and for the restrictions on meetings with his family, lawyers and political leaders to be removed, maintaining that any negligence or unnecessary restrictions concerning his health and safety would be unacceptable.

The meeting also strongly condemned the detention of Imran’s sister Aleema Khan, held since late September under Section 3 of the Maintenance of Public Order Ordinance (MPO), and demanded her immediate release.

It called for Bushra Bibi’s release as well and demanded that she be provided justice in accordance with the law.

According to the statement, the participants further demanded that cases against Dr Yasmin Rashid, Shah Mahmood Qureshi, Mahmoodur Rashid, Ejaz Chaudhry and other detained PTI leaders and workers be decided on merit, without political victimisation.

articles.title: Veteran journalist Husain Naqi passes away in Lahore
articles.summary:
LAHORE: Veteran journalist and human rights activist Husain Naqi passed away in Lahore on Sunday.

He was a former editor of The News and had also been associated with the Human Rights Commission of Pakistan (HRCP).

HRCP official Muhammad Ilyas told Dawn that Naqi died of a cardiac arrest.

“He attended a book launch ceremony at the HRCP the previous day. Later, he suffered a heart attack around 6pm on Saturday. He was admitted to a private hospital where he died early in the morning, around 5 am,” Ilyas said, adding that he had left behind three sons.

Naqi was buried in Model Town Extension in Lahore.

Meanwhile, condolences over his passing continued to pour in.

State broadcaster Radio Pakistan reported that Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif expressed “deep grief and sorrow over” Naqi’s passing and said it marked the “end of a bright chapter in journalism and democracy”.

The premier remembered Naqi as a “principled journalist who fearlessly raised voice for freedom of expression, democratic values and human rights throughout his life”.

The prime minister expressed his “heartfelt condolences to the bereaved family, the journalistic community and human rights organisations. He also prayed for the departed soul”, the Radio Pakistan report said.

President Asif Ali Zardari also extended his condolences to the bereaved family, expressing “deep sorrow”, a statement issued by the Presidency said.

The president paid tribute to Naqi’s “services to journalism, freedom of expression and human rights”, the statement said.

It further quoted the president as saying: “Husain Naqi played a prominent role in promoting journalism and democratic values. His contributions will always be remembered.”

The HRCP also released a statement, saying it “deeply mourns” Naqi’s passing.

“Over a career spanning more than 70 years, from student leader to newspaper editor to treasurer of HRCP, neither multiple incarcerations nor vindictive acts by the authorities ever weakened his resolve to speak truth to power. Naqi sahib served HRCP in different capacities for three decades and was an active council member at the time of his passing. One of the strongest voices for people’s rights and democracy in Pakistan has gone silent,” the statement said.

PPP Senator Sherry Rehman posted on X that she was “truly grieved to hear about the sad demise of the veteran journalist and rights campaigner, the iconic Husain Naqi”.

“His passing signals the end of an era. Naqi sahib always spoke unflinching truth to power. Many of us cub journalists learnt at his desk, walked in rallies under his leadership. He led so many groups and networks in the hardest days of dictatorship.

“We often called him the rebel angel of our times, yet he never stoked anger. He sought the right to dissent with respect. He will be missed. May his soul rest in peace and power,” she said.

PTI Secretary General Salman Akram Raja began his codolence on X by stating: “Alas! Naqi sahib is no longer among us.”

He said his acquaintance and admiration for Naqi spanned decades.

Naming I.A. Rehman, Asma Jahangir and Amin Mughal along with Naqi, Raja said, “The most precious gems who dreamed of and championed the dignity of human beings and the rising of voices of the poor in Pakistan are leaving us.

“Their dreams have yet to be realised. Their dreams are the dreams of 250 million people.”

Journalist Absa Komal said Naqi spent his entire life advocating for freedom of speech.

“I met him a few months ago at a conference in Karachi, and he still had the same spirit and commitment to the cause. A remarkable life,” she added.

Journalist Raza Rumi was more succinct in his message that said: “Rest in peace Naqi sahib.”

Former senator Mushahid Hussain Sayed said Naqi was the “last Icon of ‘Old Guard’ progressive journalists” who always spoke truth to power.

Who was Husain Naqi?

Naqi was born in Lucknow, India before the Independence in 1947. In his autobiography Mujh Se Jo Ho Saka, Naqi said he was perhaps born a year before his officially recorded birthdate in 1936.

His great-grandfather had moved to Lucknow from a village in what is now Haryana, in the then-undivided Punjab. It was a well-heeled and well-educated family that flourished in Lucknow over the next few generations.

However, Naqi subtly confronted the conservatism of his traditional family from a very young age. Outside, he was not subtle. He began his student activism in secondary school and started taking on the minor establishments of power at a fairly young age.

After early schooling and college education in Lucknow, Naqi moved to Karachi in the 1950s, where he developed into a student leader.

As a student in Karachi, Naqi played a key role in several demonstrations and protests. During the 1956 Suez Canal crisis when Egypt was attacked by Israel, France and Britain, Naqi was part of the executive committee of the National Students Federation (NSF). At the time, the NSF organised a march to the British High Commission in Karachi to protest against the attack and was faced with police batons and tear gas.

As president of Karachi University’s student union, Naqi made a deal with the university’s vice-chancellor for Naqi to be rusticated for three years instead of three Baloch students who had been rusticated in response to an incident at the hostel.

Naqi’s activism during his student days was not just centred around protests but also had to do with improving conditions in the institution. He fought for adding a new campus with better facilities, providing safe transport for girls and ensuring that exams were held on time and not postponed.

He was a strong advocate for student unions.

In an interview published in 2011, he said, “it was the banning of student unions that destroyed campus peace. In our time, student unions were a positive influence. We organised cultural activities. We tolerated diversity. Representatives with various political leanings were able to work together despite their ideological differences”.

After a few turbulent years in Karachi, Naqi permanently settled down in Lahore.

As a journalist, Naqi found his first mentor in Javed Bokhari, with whom he worked for a couple of years. “In those days I used to literally live at the PPI office,” he had said of the time.

He ended up working as the bureau chief of PPI. However, he eventually had to leave the position following a reporting incident in which he refused to accept a false news of desecration of the Holy Quran.

Nonetheless, he continued to write for various newspapers, including the Viewpoint, Holiday, Outlook, Frontier Post, Frontier Guardian, Daily Star, Punjab Times and Punjab Punch.

Naqi consistently campaigned for the preservation and promotion of the Punjabi language in Pakistan, starting the first-ever daily newspaper in the Punjabi language — Sajjan.

Naqi had also been imprisoned a couple of times because of his outspokenness. In the 2011 interview, he recalled those instances with a sense of humour. “I was lucky to invariably have someone favourably disposed towards me at the jail premises, who made sure that I was not mistreated.”

articles.title: Pakistani among two injured in Iranian attacks, Bahrain says
articles.summary:
A Pakistani citizen was among two injured in last night’s Iranian attacks on Bahrain, authorities in the kingdom said on Sunday.

The Gulf kingdom has suffered several attacks this week, ending a weeks-long lull in the conflict that began with US-Israeli strikes on Iran in late February.

In a statement late on Saturday night, Bahrain’s interior ministry accused Tehran of striking a “civilian industrial facility”, without specifying the location. It said the incident caused fire and material damage, but no injuries were reported.

The ministry later issued another alert of a “potential threat“, giving an all-clear after midnight local time.

In a subsequent statement on Sunday, the interior ministry said: “As a result of the heinous Iranian attacks on Bahrain yesterday, a Bahraini citizen with disabilities sustained injuries and is in stable condition, while a Pakistani resident was also injured and is in critical condition.

“Both are receiving treatment in the hospital,” it added.

Residents told AFP they saw smoke rising over Sitra Island, on Bahrain’s east coast, home to several industrial sites including a refinery run by state oil company Bapco.

Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps (IRGC) said that “during the operation, US military positions at the Al-Riffa and Awali bases in Bahrain were targeted with missile and drone strikes”.

“Two radars belonging to the US Army’s Patriot air defence systems… were struck,” it said, adding that any violation of Iranian airspace will be met with a “harsh and decisive response”.

The attacks came as two tankers were struck in the Strait of Hormuz, which has become the focus of the stalemated conflict, with Iran continuing its efforts to blockade the strategic shipping lane.

The US military, meanwhile, has been escorting ships through the strategic strait, which carried about one-fifth of the world’s oil before the war, and maintains its own counterblockade of Iranian ports.

British maritime agency UKMTO said on Saturday one tanker was struck by an “unknown projectile” while transiting Hormuz. “There are no reported casualties at this time,” it said, adding another tanker was hit in its engine room.

Tehran has repeatedly reported ships catching fire in the strait in recent weeks, often claiming they struck mines.

Iranian deputy foreign minister Kazem Gharibabadi said on Saturday that a Qatari delegation visited Tehran the previous evening and “held two hours of talks”, without providing details.

Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said: “The ongoing talks in the region must be given a chance, and the blockade must be lifted rationally.”

“Our position is clear: as long as Iran’s demands are not met, the discussion on the Strait of Hormuz and its opening is pointless,” he said, quoted by state TV.

Iran’s demands include ending the war on all fronts, unfreezing Iranian assets, lifting oil sanctions and ending the US counter-blockade of Iranian ports.

‘Clear red lines’

Washington announced what it called an “economic asphyxiation” campaign on Iran in August aimed at curbing its trade and financial flows.

Gharibabadi said on Saturday, according to Iran’s Tasnim news agency, that “we consider the economic blockade an act of war and we will take all necessary measures to lift it”.

“We have made this known to the other parties, including the mediators”, he added, saying “the United States was aware of this.”

In an interview published on Saturday by the state-run Iran Daily newspaper, Araghchi reiterated that Tehran would not allow its stockpiles of enriched uranium to leave the country.

The Iranian nuclear programme is one of the major issues in Iranian-American relations. Western nations accuse Iran of seeking a bomb, though Tehran insists the programme is entirely civilian in nature.

“I believe a solution can be found, but we have clear red lines: the material will not be taken out of the country,” Araghchi said.

Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, meanwhile, said US and Israeli strikes on Iran’s energy infrastructure had exacerbated energy problems, “and we should therefore expect difficulties this winter”.

Mohammad Allahdad, head of Iran’s national electricity company, told state TV that the country will impose rolling power cuts from Sunday.

“Given the country’s fuel supply conditions, the electricity sector will be forced to impose distribution restrictions,” he said.

articles.title: PPP, PML-N spat continues as Asif's jibe at Bilawal draws 'red line' warning
articles.summary:
In the latest from the ongoing wrangling between the ruling PML-N and its ally in the Centre, the PPP, leaders from the latter have said Defence Minister Khawaja Asif’s remarks directed at Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari were “unacceptable” and crossed the party’s “red line”.

The reaction from PPP Senator Sherry Rehman and MNA Sharmila Faruqui on Sunday came on a Nov 19 post by Asif, in which he shared two video clips of PPP Chairperson Bilawal.

In the first clip, Bilawal is seen criticising the PTI and its founder, Imran Khan, and in the second one, from his recent address at the Karachi Press Club (KPC), he terms Imran a “political prisoner”.

“A person becomes the prime minister and is later imprisoned. So I can either accept that every prime minister in the country’s history has been a thief, or I can accept that all prime ministers in our history have been victims of political revenge,” he adds.

Commenting on the two clips, Asif posted on X: “We believed that the new generation would be better and more principled than ours. Did not know they would turn out to be masters of dishonesty and change colours so remarkably.”

Reacting to his remarks, Rehman posted on X: “Unacceptable flow of comments from the federal defence minister about the PPP organisation and our leadership, Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari. He has crossed a red line.”

Similarly, Faruqui said Asif’s “derogatory language”, particularly his “irresponsible remarks” about Bilawal, were unacceptable for the PPP.

“This is a red line for us.”

Directly addressing Asif, she went on to say that while everyone had the right to disagree politically, there was a difference between derision and disagreement.

“As a senior parliamentarian and a federal minister, you are expected to exercise political judgement, seriousness and decorum. Political differences are addressed through reasoned argument, not personal attacks. Remember, words reflect not only a person’s character but also the dignity of their office.”

The PPP and the PML-N have been trading barbs after Bilawal speech at the KPC on Nov 17. On the occasion, the Bhutto scion addressed the ongoing debate on the creation of new provinces, expressed support for several opposition demands and questioned past decisions and actions taken by the ruling coalition. He also warned of bloodshed in Sindh over the creation of new provinces and called for a “political reset”.

His remarks drew a strong reaction from senior leaders of the PML-N, Jamaat-i-Islami (JI) and Muttahida Qaumi Movement-Pakistan, who accused him of “political hypocrisy”.

Asif continued his criticism of Bilawal on Saturday, accusing him of being the “biggest beneficiary and a critic of the system at the same time”.

“Rank opportunism,” he commented.

Earlier, he brought the ownership of Bilawal House in Lahore into the political argument.

In a post on X, the defence minister questioned the ownership and use of Bilawal House, asking: “Can someone disclose the ownership of this property? Who owns it, and who lives there? If this palace-like fortress is being used by anyone, who are they?”

The PML-N senior leader further questioned whether those occupying properties without having legal title to them could “morally claim any privileged position”, adding that the 250 million people of Pakistan deserved to know the financial and property details of those who considered high status and privilege their entitlement.

Responding to him, PPP senior leader Nadeem Afzal Chan posted a video showing party workers gathering at the Bilawal House in Lahore, saying the property was the home of every PPP worker. “Show us people entering any other big house in the same way. Uncle… answer the questions, whether you like it or not,” Chan said in his X post, directly addressing the defence minister.

Separately, the PPP accused the defence minister of attempting to provoke the party into launching personal attacks against the PML-N leadership in retaliation. In a statement posted on X, the PPP said Bilawal had directed party leaders to ignore the defence minister’s remarks and concentrate on issue-based politics.

The statement, however, warned that the PPP was also familiar with the political controversies surrounding the PML-N leadership, referring to the Panama Papers, Avenfield properties and Al-Azizia Steel Mills cases.

However, even as the heated exchange of words continued between the two sides, President Asif Ali Zardari and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif had decided that all matters would be resolved through dialogue, the Presidency said on Thursday after the two leaders met in Islamabad.

The two again met on Saturday to discuss the overall political situation.

After the meeting, Rehman urged the government to focus on people’s problems rather than creating new political fault lines.

Provocative statements by ministers should be avoided, she said, adding that Bilawal wanted politics to address people’s problems rather than create new divisions.

“Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari is looking to prevent bloodshed, not shed it,” she said.

articles.title: Lahore once again ranks as world's most polluted major city as AQI crosses 500
articles.summary:
Lahore topped the list of the world’s most polluted major cities once again on Sunday morning with an hourly air quality index (AQI) reading of over 500, according to real-time air quality data.

Swiss air quality monitoring platform IQAir’s live global major city ranking placed Lahore first with 538 between 9am and 10am, classifying the quality as ‘hazardous’, indicating extremely polluted conditions and serious health risks for residents.

It was followed by Delhi with an AQI of 207, Karachi with 180, Mumbai with 177 and Cairo at 162. The ranking showed Lahore’s pollution level to be more than twice that of the second-ranked city, Delhi.

The deterioration was not confined to the provincial capital.

IQAir’s live ranking of Pakistani cities on Sunday morning placed eight Punjab cities among the country’s 10 most polluted urban centres.

Kahna Nau in Lahore district topped the list with an AQI of 606, followed by Lahore at 538, Bahawalpur at 536, Sargodha at 392 and Gujranwala at 347.

Other cities in the top 10 included Multan, Dera Ghazi Khan, Skardu, Faisalabad and Peshawar.

IQ Air rankings for the most polluted cities on Nov 22. — Screengrab IQAir

According to global health statistics, air pollution, both outdoor and indoor, is the second-leading risk factor for deaths worldwide, claiming an estimated 8.1 million lives annually. Outdoor particulate matter alone accounts for 4.7m deaths.

Lahore has consistently ranked as the world’s most polluted major city in the past few weeks. On Saturday evening, it recorded an AQI of 266, showing Lahore’s air quality in the hazardous category.

On Friday, heavy smog pushed air quality in several Punjab cities into the hazardous category, with Lahore recording an hourly AQI reading of 465 between 7am and 8am.

Punjab govt intensifies crackdown against smog violations

Amid the worsening air quality, Punjab’s Environment Protection and Climate Change Department (EPCCD) has intensified its province-wide crackdown against environmental violations, imposing fines amounting to Rs449.5 million, sealing 6,476 premises and carrying out 1,808 demolitions during the first 11 months of 2026.

According to the latest enforcement figures compiled by the Environment Protection Agency (EPA) Punjab, enforcement teams conducted 187,588 field visits across the province between January 1 and November 21, targeting industrial pollution, non-compliant brick kilns, illegal plastic businesses, commercial establishments and fugitive dust.

The enforcement drive has also yielded a 60 per cent increase in fines compared with the corresponding period last year, reflecting intensified regulatory action against major sources of pollution.

Industrial units accounted for the largest share of penalties, with fines reaching Rs231.6 million against Rs108.8m during the same period in 2025.

Brick kilns attracted Rs183.3m in fines, while penalties against plastic-related violations increased 4.5 times to Rs34.5 million.

Brick kiln inspections remained a major component of the campaign, with 85,768 visits recorded during the reporting period. Enforcement teams demolished 1,431 units and sealed another 1,018 premises. Industrial enforcement operations involved 50,555 inspections, resulting in 1,525 premises being sealed and 377 demolitions.

The department has also stepped up enforcement against restaurants and commercial establishments operating without the required suction hoods. A total of 10,766 inspections were conducted, leading to the installation of 4,385 suction hoods and the sealing of 1,287 premises. Significantly, 1,130 suction hoods were installed during November alone.

The daily enforcement figures for November 21 further illustrated the scale of operations, with teams conducting 1,022 inspections across Punjab and imposing fines of Rs1.87 million.

The operation resulted in 20 premises being sealed, seven FIRs registered and one brick kiln demolished. Officials also confiscated 390 kilogrammes of plastic bags and oversaw the installation of 72 suction hoods.

Brick kilns accounted for 499 of the day’s inspections, followed by 275 industrial units, 153 plastic-related inspections and 95 suction-hood inspections. All seven FIRs and the demolition recorded on the day were related to brick kilns.

Director General Environment Abdullah Nayyar Sheikh said the department was maintaining strict enforcement against all major sources of pollution through continuous monitoring, field inspections and action against non-compliant units. He emphasised that the strategy was aimed at ensuring compliance with environmental laws and preventing pollution at its source.

EPCCD Secretary Silwat Saeed also stressed the importance of sustained institutional monitoring and effective implementation of environmental regulations to address pollution through a coordinated enforcement approach.

A day earlier, the Lahore Traffic Police claimed to have intensified enforcement operations against vehicles contributing to air pollution.

Chief Traffic Officer Syed Abdul Rahim Shirazi on Saturday claimed that the traffic police have issued challan tickets to 14,653 smoke-emitting vehicles.

Action has also been taken against 10,306 vehicles transporting sand, soil and other materials without covering their loads with tarpaulins. The police have also proceeded against 31,618 unfit and dilapidated vehicles and taken action against 272,760 vehicles for overloading, he said.

Pakistan’s average PM2.5 concentration stood at 67.3 micrograms per cubic metre in 2025, nearly 14 times the World Health Organisation’s annual guideline of 5 micrograms per cubic metre, according to the 2025 World Air Quality Report.

This concentration corresponded to an average AQI of 156, placing Pakistan among the world’s most polluted countries.

articles.title: Presidential ordinance withdraws most privileges of KP MPAs, including protection against preventive detention
articles.summary:
PESHAWAR: President Asif Ali Zardari has promulgated five ordinances, doing away with most of the “privileges” of the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa lawmakers, including protection against “preventive detention” and providing a legal framework for special initiatives in the designated 12 districts and other districts in the province.

With the imposition of emergency in KP on Oct 11, an Area Representative and Development Council (ARDC) was formed to oversee 12 districts that were deemed to face intense security challenges, including the merged districts.

Two of the ordinances envisage setting up an executive committee with wide-ranging powers to oversee special initiatives, including developmental schemes, in the 12 designated districts and the rest of the province, respectively.

The committee will have powers to identify and recommend the executing agency for special initiatives in the designated and other districts, including military formations.

In a statement on Saturday, President Zardari’s office confirmed he had promulgated five ordinances pertaining to KP. Of these, the following four had been published in the Official Gazette on Nov 19 after their promulgation:

Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Societies (Registration) (Amendment) Ordinance, 2026;

Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Special Initiative Ordinance, 2026 (specific districts);

Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Special Initiative Ordinance, 2026 (other districts);

Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Provincial Assembly (Powers, Immunities and Privileges) Ordinance, 2026 (XI of 2026).

The fifth was the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Speaker and Deputy Speaker (Salaries, Allowances and Privileges) Ordinance 2026.

Through the amendment ordinance related to privileges of MPAs, drastic changes have been made in the KP Provincial Assembly (Powers, Immunities and Privileges) Act 2026, as 21 of its 40 sections have been omitted, including those providing protection to the MPAs against “preventive detentions” and offences related to “breach” of privileges.

The schedule of offences related to “breach of privileges” of the Assembly, its members and committees has also been omitted, thus leaving them without significant privileges.

It may be mentioned that Sohail Afridi — whose role as the chief minister was rendered non-functional due to governor’s rule — Speaker Babar Saleem Swati and other lawmakers have been in “preventive detention” since emergency was imposed, according to police.

KP Governor Faisal Karim Kundi also said last month that they had been placed under house arrest.

The important provisions omitted through the ordinance include sections 5 (attendance of MPA detained or arrested), 6 (members not liable to civil or criminal action), 10 (preventive detention), 11 (permission of speaker before arrest, detention, etc. of a member), 15 (power to summon), 22 (power to arrest), 31 (breach of privilege), 32 (breach of privilege to be an offence) and 34 (cognisance of offence).

Special initiative ordinances

The two ordinances relate to special initiatives in the 12 designated districts and the remaining districts in the province, respectively.

Both the ordinances provide for the establishment of an executive committee comprising a chairman, vice chairman and other such members as nominated by the prime minister, in case of designated district, and by the governor of the province, in case of the remaining districts.

For the designated districts, the Area Development Secretariat shall serve as secretariat of the executive committee, whereas for the other districts, the planning and development department shall serve as the secretariat of the committee.

Under the new laws, “special initiative” includes any work, developmental scheme, rehabilitation or reconstruction work, procurement of goods and human resources, consulting or non-consulting services or any other activity involving expenditure of public funds as determined by the executive committee.

The executive committee, in both the ordinances, has extensive powers including:

Identify an initiative as a special initiative of urgent or emergent nature;

Scrutinise and approve proposals, concept papers and PC-Is for the special initiatives;

Grant anticipatory approval for the initiatives, proposals, concept papers and PC-Is of the special initiatives;

Identify and recommend the executing agency, including military organisations and formations, for the execution of the special initiatives;

Provide a mechanism for the monitoring and evaluation of the special initiatives, including third-party monitoring and evaluation;

Review progress of the special initiatives;

Constitute committees or designate persons to carry out functions assigned to them by the executive committee;

Perform any other act to carry out the purposes of the ordinance.

The ordinances provide that the executive committee should meet at least once a month or as and when required.

The decisions of the committee shall be made on the basis of majority vote of its members, and in case of a tie, the chairman shall have the casting vote.

The chairman is also empowered to co-opt any other member or technical expert, to offer advice to the committee, as required.

Both the ordinances have overriding effect on other laws, including the KP Public Procurement Regulatory Authority Act 2012 and the KP Public Private Partnership Act 2020.

Moreover, no civil court shall have jurisdiction in relation to an act done, order passed, and any proceedings done under the ordinances.

Madressah registrations

Through the KP Societies (Registration) (Amendment) Ordinance, 2026, a sub-section 1-A has been included in Section 21, dealing with the registration of “religious madressahs”.

The newly included provision provides that madressahs which are or may be registered with the Directorate General of Religious Education, Ministry of Federal Education and Professional Training, shall not be required to be registered under the Act (Societies Registration Act).

articles.title: Broken record: UN entry, Mountbatten’s prejudice and the Grand Mufti’s letter
articles.summary:
Pakistan’s long and fruitful association with the United Nations began formally in the last week of September, as its application for UN membership was accepted. In other major developments, Louis Mountbatten was accused of throwing Muslim employees in Delhi under the bus, while the Grand Mufti of Jerusalem, Haj Amin Al Hussaini, issued a fervent appeal through Dawn to highlight Palestine’s plight.

UN membership

There were two major diplomatic achievements for Pakistan in the last week of September. The first was the young country’s acceptance as a member of the UN, then known as the United Nations Organisation (UNO). This was no small feat, as membership announced that Pakistan was ready to take its place in the comity of nations.

‘Dominion of Pakistan unanimously accepted for UNO membership’, the headline from the Sept 26 edition read. Pakistan received all 35 votes, though an interesting procedural question was raised by the Argentine representative. The report filed from Lake Success, NY (where the UN was based before shifting to its current headquarters in Manhattan in 1951), said: “The Dominion of Pakistan was unanimously recommended for membership in the UNO … by the Political Committee of the General Assembly. The resolution received the committee’s full 35 votes, but only after the Argentine delegate, Senor Jose Arce, objected to the necessity for Pakistan to apply for membership at all.”

Of course Senor Arce held no malice towards Pakistan; in fact he wanted to introduce Pakistan as a Charter member (India was already a Charter member, having joined the UN while still a British colony in 1945). As the report pointed out, “it was clear in the course of the debate that nobody was questioning the present status of India as member of the UNO, or the desirability of Pakistan becoming a member. … [The question] was whether a member of the UNO, if split into two separate nations, would create a situation in which two seats in the UNO were automatically available.

“The Argentine’s case was that either Pakistan and India were both automatically members, or that neither were members until they had been formally admitted.”

Thankfully the diplomatic debate was resolved amicably, and Pakistan was admitted. It was interesting to note that despite the intense Partition-related violence, the Indian delegation, which was present during the debate, did not oppose Pakistan’s membership. Perhaps, on one level, those were more civil times.

Washington’s man in Karachi

Another major diplomatic development during this period was the appointment of America’s first ambassador to Pakistan. As detailed in a report in the Sept 24 edition, US President Harry S. Truman appointed Mr Paul H. Alling as Washington’s first envoy to Pakistan.

Unlike many of the questionable characters that the current White House has posted at foreign missions, Mr Alling was a seasoned diplomat. Washington’s man in Karachi had sterling credentials, as he was chief of the State Department’s division of Near Eastern affairs, while he had also advised the American delegation to the UNO.

Moreover, Mr Alling had served as US Consul in Beirut, Syria as well as other posts in the Middle East. Meanwhile, Pakistan’s first ambassador to the US, tycoon and diplomat Mirza Abol Hassan (M.A.H.) Ispahani, had already arrived in America.

The appointment of the American ambassador would mark the start of one of Pakistan’s most important — and most complex — foreign relationships.

Mountbatten’s prejudice?

Louis Mountbatten, the last British viceroy of India, is known to have had cool relations with Quaid-i-Azam Mohammad Ali Jinnah, while enjoying cordial ties with Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru. ‘Dickie’ Mountbatten was apparently slighted by the fact that the Quaid chose to be the first Governor-General of Pakistan, whereas the Indians readily accepted him for the same post in their country. But did this bitterness turn Mountbatten into a prejudiced man? A report from the Sept 28 edition seems to suggest so.

Titled ‘Sack Muslim staffs, says Mountbatten to diplomats’, the report says that “Lord Mountbatten sent for all the foreign diplomats stationed in Hindustan’s capital … and told them that they should immediately get rid of their Muslim employees.

“They were told that if they sheltered Muslims or gave protection to their own employees, the Government of India would not be responsible for their safety.”

It added that “all these diplomats sent their Muslim employees and domestic servants to the various refugee camps. … It is also significant that Lord Mountbatten was not able to protect his own Muslim employees and domestic servants, some of whom were killed and wounded.”

If these reports are true, they would shatter the myth of empire being a benevolent, benign force, and expose it as ruthless and vengeful, even in its dying days.

Grand Mufti’s letter

This newspaper’s commitment to the Palestinian cause goes back to the time of Independence. In fact, Haj Amin Al-Hussaini, the Grand Mufti of Al-Quds, had written to Dawn asking the paper to raise awareness about Palestine’s plight.

As chronicled in the Sept 28 issue, Haj Amin wrote that “Undoubtedly you know the dangers threatening Palestine because of the Zionist imperialistic aims, and because of the decisions of the United Nations’ Special Committee on Palestine in dividing Palestine into two States — an Arab and a Jewish — although the majority of the Jews in Palestine are foreigners who entered Palestine by force of British arms after the British occupation.

“We are in urgent need of your help to raise your strong voice in disapproving the UNSCOP report and to do your best in order to save Palestine, the first Qiblah and the third Masjid from the dangers threatening her.”

Haj Amin was a prescient man and could see what was coming for his people. Sadly, 79 years after the Mufti’s impassioned appeal, the people of Palestine continue to suffer from Zionist terrorism.

With the advantage of hindsight, one has the opportunity to study the historical cycles in a nation’s life. Thanks to this newspaper’s unique, extensive archive of back issues, one can examine the major political, economic and social trends that have shaped Pakistan and the world over the last seven decades and counting. Cliched as it may sound, history repeats itself, and we — as a state and as a polity — largely refuse to learn from it.

Through this platform, we will look back at the ‘big’ stories that made it to the front pages of Dawn, as well as significant developments tucked away in the inside pages, from the birth of Pakistan onwards, and try to put them in perspective. We will study the critical issues of the week, starting from Aug 14, 1947 and examine the major themes and issues that made it to the paper.

articles.title: Forensic evidence points to servant in Hina Javaid murder as probe clears husband
articles.summary:
• After nearly three-month delay, police submit charge sheet in high-profile murder case
• According to the DNA analysis report, Hina Javaid was reportedly sexually assaulted after being murdered by her domestic servant

RAWALPINDI: Rawalpindi police have completed their investigation into the high-profile murder of digital media executive Hina Javaid, who was found dead with signs of torture and strangulation at her husband’s apartment in Lal Kurti in August. The police submitted the challan to the court after about three months.

The development was disclosed by newly appointed City Police Officer (CPO) Rawalpindi Sardar Ghias Gul during his first interaction with media persons on Saturday.

Hina Javaid was murdered on August 20, 2026, at her husband’s house, and her domestic servant has been identified as the main suspect in the case following a forensic DNA match and a report by a high-level inquiry committee.

Hina Javaid’s husband and his father have been cleared of any involvement in the murder by the police investigation, as no evidence linking them to the crime has been found.

At one point during the course of investigation, Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz noted that “DNA test results and polygraph test suggest that the murder and rape were committed by the servant.”

However, he said the investigation was ongoing. On Oct 29, First Lady Aseefa Bhutto Zardari also met with Hina’s family at the Parliament and called for the family’s demand for a judicial commission to be “given due consideration”.

Although Hina Javaid’s husband and her father-in-law were named in the initial FIR registered on murder charges, they were given a clean chit in the police investigation. However, Hina’s husband was arrested, while her father-in-law was only questioned by the police.

It will be up to the court to decide whether Hina’s husband and father-in-law had any link to her murder. The police are required to submit a challan in a murder case within 15 days after a suspect is sent to judicial remand.

Meanwhile, Hina’s family had expressed dissatisfaction over the police investigation and demanded a judicial inquiry.

The family claimed to have proof of evidence tampering by the husband’s brother, who allegedly cleaned the accused’s room, tampered with evidence, and colluded with the police.

The police have already added Section 376 of the Pakistan Penal Code (rape) to the case following the forensic DNA findings.

CPO Sardar Ghias Gul told media persons that the challan had been submitted to the court for legal proceedings. He also acknowledged shortcomings in police prosecution, which result in the release of criminals, and said these would be addressed by appointing the right people to the right positions.

The Punjab government had constituted a three-member high-powered committee to review the investigation into the murder case, in which her husband and a domestic servant had been placed on judicial remand at Adiala Jail.

As part of the investigation, the committee also visited the crime scene, questioned the deceased woman’s husband and the domestic servant in jail, and met members of her family.

The committee comprises Additional Inspector General of the Crime Control Department (CCD) Sohail Chattha, DIG Lahore Shoaib Khurram Janbaz and SSP Investigation Rawalpindi Saifullah.

Published in Dawn, November 22nd, 2026

articles.title: Summonses for India’s security czar, ex-spymaster sent to Delhi court
articles.summary:
WASHINGTON: A US federal court has sent legal summonses for Indian National Security Adviser Ajit Doval and former Research and Analysis Wing (R&AW) chief Samant Goel to three district courts in New Delhi, seeking assistance in serving them in a civil lawsuit alleging Indian government conspiracy to assassinate Sikh nationalist leader Gurpatwant Singh Pannun.

US District Judge Katherine Polk Failla authorised the transmission of the legal documents through the Indian judicial system, after earlier attempts to serve them through India’s designated central authority and diplomatic channels failed.

The summonses were sent by FedEx on Friday to Patiala House, Dwarka and Tis Hazari court complexes under provisions of the 1965 Hague Convention and India’s Code of Civil Procedure. The Patiala House district court was requested to facilitate service on Doval, while the Dwarka and Tis Hazari courts were approached in connection with Goel.

US district judge allows alternative way after previous attempts failed in Pannun case

The lawsuit, filed in September 2024, alleges that Indian officials conspired to arrange Pannun’s assassination in New York. It names the Indian government, Doval, Goel, former R&AW officer Vikram Yadav, Indian national Nikhil Gupta and 50 unidentified individuals as defendants. Pannun is seeking damages, alleging that the defendants conspired to arrange his assassination in retaliation for his advocacy of an independent Sikh state of Khalistan.

The legal route was considered after the Indian Ministry of Law and Justice, the country’s designated central authority for processing foreign requests under the Hague Convention, returned the documents. The authority stated that the summonses did not fall within the specified categories.

The US judge, however, held that the Indian authority’s brief response did not establish that the Hague Convention was inapplicable to the case. She concluded that Article 19 nevertheless permitted the use of India’s domestic judicial procedures.

Previous attempts to serve Doval personally during his visits to the United States had also failed, according to court filings. Pannun’s lawyers told the court that security personnel had prevented them from delivering the documents on three occasions.

While rejecting the lawsuit, India’s External Affairs Ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal reiterated New Delhi’s position, saying: “I have said earlier that we reject such baseless lawsuits.”

Earlier on Nov 10, Jaiswal had described the allegations against senior Indian officials as fabricated and malicious and maintained that requests for serving judicial documents in India could only be routed through the Ministry of Law and Justice.

The case has acquired renewed significance following the conviction and sentencing of Gupta in a separate US criminal proceeding on Friday. The federal court in New York sentenced Gupta to nearly 20 years in prison after he pleaded guilty in February 2026 to participating in a murder-for-hire conspiracy targeting Pannun.

According to US prosecutors, Yadav, an Indian government employee associated with the Cabinet Secretariat that houses India’s intelligence service, had recruited Gupta in 2023 to arrange Pannun’s killing in New York.

Prosecutors said Yadav agreed to pay $100,000 for the assassination, with $15,000 delivered as an advance payment. Gupta was arrested in the Czech Republic in June 2023 and extradited to the United States in 2024.

Yadav has also been charged in the criminal case but remains outside US custody.

articles.title: Punjab land reforms project reaches 90pc progress
articles.summary:
ISLAMABAD: The World Bank-fin­a­n­ced Punjab Urban Land Systems Enhan­cement (Pulse) project has achieved 90 per cent physical progress, recording 69.9 million land rights in its information system against a target of 50.7 million, with 31pc registered in women’s names.

According to the project’s progress report, all activities are expected to be completed by its closing date in June 2027.

Updated digital cadastral maps now cover around 86pc of Punjab, while about 31 million person-based land records have been converted into parcel-based records.

Of the province’s 6,014 revenue villages (mauzas), 5,805 have been digitised and notified, 27 have been submitted for notification and work remains in 182.

World Bank-funded scheme digitises 5,805 revenue villages, with completion targeted for June 2027

The project covers more than 24.4m landowners. Under its mass partition initiative, 495,163 of the 1,747,071 eligible jointly owned land holdings have been divided, creating around 1.18m new parcels. Of these, 94,833 have been registered in women’s names. The Green Property Certificate survey has received 46,626 applications, completed 37,272 field assessments, approved 23,280 cases and issued 54,694 certificates.

The project has also filled 346 positions across its management units. As of October, disbursements stood at around $91.84m, or 61.8pc of the total credit, the report said.

Approved in 2022 with financing of $150m, the project aims to establish a unified land registry linked to digital cadastral maps, forming the basis of a comprehensive land administration system covering urban and rural areas of Punjab.

Growing urban challenges

The province has a population of around 110m, of which 36.7pc lives in urban areas. Urban growth is largely driven by migration from rural areas, with 60pc of recent migrants to Punjab’s urban centres coming from rural areas.

The report identifies several environmental and social challenges in urban and peri-urban areas, including air pollution, contaminated drinking water, untreated wastewater, inadequate solid waste collection and disposal, and the expansion of cities over prime agricultural land.

It also highlights public health probl­e­ms, particularly water-borne diseases, unequal access to basic services, weak tra­nsparency and accountability, and low public satisfaction with service delivery. Government agencies lack up-to-date information about public land that could be used for housing and other developm­ent projects. Land acquisition can take up to five years on average, it says.

articles.title: Referendum is no substitute for legislation: PTI
articles.summary:
• Challenges Bilawal to return reserved seats, remove Kundi
• Accuses PPP leadership of playing ‘good cop, bad cop’

ISLAMABAD: The PTI on Saturday dismissed proposals for a referendum on new provinces as an absurd and futile exercise that could not replace a majority vote or a constitutional bill in the national or provincial assemblies, while urging PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari to return reserved seats to the party and remove Faisal Karim Kundi as Khyber Pakhtunkhwa governor.

In a statement, PTI Central Information Secretary Sheikh Waqas Akram said floating the idea of a referendum instead of introducing legislation in parliament validated the party’s long-standing position that the sitting assemblies lacked legitimacy and had been formed on a “stolen mandate and usurped seats” through Form-47 results.

“Because the current lawmakers are not true public representatives, any referendum held under the present setup would be as fraudulent as the assembly itself,” he claimed.

Outlining the PTI’s internal consultation process, Mr Akram said the issue of a referendum would be deliberated upon by the parliamentary party, political committee and core committee, though the final authority rested solely with incarcerated PTI founder Imran Khan.

He made it clear that the PTI would formulate its policy on the creation of new provinces only after party leaders were granted direct access to Imran Khan, whose approval would be final.

He noted that while Imran Khan and the PTI had consistently advocated smaller administrative units, the party would never endorse decisions imposed without constitutional legitimacy, democratic consensus and public consent. He warned that imposing governments on people who had rejected them would defeat the purpose of administrative reform.

The PTI information secretary expressed gratitude to Mr Bhutto-Zardari for expressing concern over the health of Imran Khan, demanding his release and calling him a political prisoner. He said the PTI thanked all those who had spoken out against the “unjust” treatment meted out to the party founder.

Turning his attention to the PPP leadership, Mr Akram said President Asif Ali Zardari had always engaged in the politics of expediency and claimed that the father-son duo was currently playing a good cop, bad cop routine that the public recognised well. While acknowledging the PPP chairman’s recent, belated admission of harsh political realities, he stressed that words alone could not establish credibility without a clear break from the government’s “unconstitutional” measures.

Challenge to Bilawal

To prove his sincerity and show that his remarks were not merely an attempt to extract political concessions or a greater share in government, Mr Akram challenged Mr Bhutto-Zardari to take two immediate confidence-building measures: ensure the return of all usurped reserved seats to the PTI and remove Faisal Karim Kundi as KP governor or expel him from the PPP to prove that the party no longer supported measures against the province’s elected government.

He argued that the PPP could not absolve itself of responsibility for the coercion and mistreatment faced by the PTI while remaining part of the ruling arrangement.

Reflecting on the past three years, Mr Akram said systematic electoral manipulation, undue interference and controversial constitutional amendments had virtually paralysed parliament and the judiciary. He noted that even a major government ally had refused to openly endorse the amendments.

Genuine democratic change, he emphasised, required respect for the people’s electoral mandate, ensuring that parliament served the public and allowing the judiciary to rule on merit.

He condemned the disappearance of former KP finance minister Taimur Saleem Jhagra from a police station following his arrest, alongside the arrests of Irfan Saleem and Kamran Bangash, calling these incidents an extreme manifestation of lawlessness.

He reiterated the PTI’s demand that Imran Khan, his wife Bushra Bibi, non-functional KP chief minister Sohail Afridi, provincial assembly speaker Babar Saleem Swati, former Gilgit-Baltistan chief minister Khalid Khurshid Khan, Taimur Saleem Jhagra and all other detained leaders and workers be immediately presented before the courts and released without delay. He asserted that they were being targeted solely for upholding constitutional supremacy and the rule of law.

articles.title: Focus on public issues, avoid new fault lines: PPP
articles.summary:
President Asif Ali Zardari meets with Deputy Prime Minister Ishaq Dar and National Assembly Speaker Sardar Ayaz Sadiq at the Presidency.—X/PresOfPakistan

ISLAMABAD: Seeking to ease tensions between her party and PML-N amid the ongoing debate on need for new provinces, PPP Vice President Senator Sherry Rehman on Saturday urged the government to focus on people’s problems rather than create new political fault lines.

Provocative statements by ministers should be avoided, she said, adding that PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari wanted politics to address people’s problems rather than create new divisions.

“Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari is looking to prevent bloodshed, not shed it,” she said.

Her statement came before Deputy Prime Minister Ishaq Dar and National Assembly Speaker Sardar Ayaz Sadiq met President Asif Ali Zardari at President House to discuss the overall political situation. Besides Senator Rehman, PPP leader Raja Pervez Ashraf was also present.

The meeting followed an apparent easing of tensions between President Zardari and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif who also discussed the matter with Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi after the PPP chairman’s remarks at a ‘Meet the Press’ event at the Karachi Press Club. He had opposed the creation of new provinces, warning that dividing Sindh would lead to bloodshed.

He also criticised the coalition over several issues, including the treatment of JUI-F chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman, PTI founder Imran Khan’s incarceration and the 27th Amendment. He later clarified that he was raising an alarm, not issuing a threat, and complained that the PPP was not being consulted.

The remarks drew sharp reactions from PML-N ministers Khawaja Asif and Tallal Chaudhry, while MQM-P chief Khalid Maqbool Siddiqui urged the courts to take notice. Mustafa Kamal also criticised Mr Bhutto-Zardari.

President Zardari subsequently met Prime Minister Shehbaz and Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi, with the meeting calling for dialogue and restraint in public statements.

A separate PPP meeting reaffirmed the party’s opposition to Sindh’s division. A meeting between Mr Bhutto-Zardari and the prime minister is also expected in the coming days.

Senator Rehman also warned of a difficult winter, with gas and resource shortages and extreme weather in many areas, urging politicians not to add to people’s troubles by creating new fault lines.

Constitutional process

She also drew a constitutional line on demands by some ministers for a referendum on new provinces. “They [the ministers] should know that the Constitution will still refer the matter to parliament. There is no walking away from the votes of the assemblies.

A referendum does not override the Constitution, nor does it change any ground reality where any given province has spoken with its majority,” she said.

The PPP’s message was that it wanted the truce to hold but would oppose the creation of new provinces outside the constitutional parliamentary process.

Whether the easing of tensions lasts will depend on whether the parties pursue consultation and consensus through parliament or revive the referendum debate.

articles.title: Trump intends to secure ‘permanent deal’ with Iran
articles.summary:
• Araghchi says Tehran seeks ‘honourable, dignified’ agreement; says China, Russia oppose change in nuclear doctrine
• Trump envoys discuss mediation with Qatari officials
• Two tankers catch fire in Strait of Hormuz

WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump has said he intends to secure a “permanent” deal with Iran, insisting that no future American president should be able to allow Tehran to obtain a nuclear weapon, according to an Anadolu Agency report.

Speaking in a phone interview with Fox News on Saturday, Trump said his approach was shaped by what he described as “Iran’s repeated failure” to honour agreements. “We make a deal, and then they break the deal the next day,” he said, arguing that any new agreement must prevent Iran from developing nuclear weapons regardless of who occupies the White House in the coming years.

Reuters quoted the US president as telling Fox News that he’s “going to make a deal that is permanent”.

He added that he would not allow a fut­ure administration to reverse course and permit Iran to acquire a nuclear weapon.

Trump also addressed suggestions that Washington was pursuing regime change in Tehran, saying his administration had already dealt with successive groups of Iranian leadership.

“We’re dealing with the third group, so you could call that the ultimate regime change,” he said, adding that the current figures were “probably … more reasonable” but remained difficult to negotiate with.

Guarantees sought

On the other hand, Iran’s Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi told the state-owned Iran newspaper that messages continued to be exchanged between Tehran and Washington through mediators, and that Tehran was seeking “an agreement that would ensure there was no further war”.

He also said Iran wanted guarantees that Washington was serious about negotiations before proceeding further, adding that Iran had discussed with mediators the form and nature of confidence-building measures.

He also said China and Russia oppose a change in Tehran’s nuclear doctrine, amid domestic calls for a shift. He told the state-run Iran Daily that the issue was “broad, serious” and had its own “supporters and opponents”.

“Russia and China are also opposed” to a change in Iran’s doctrine, he added.

The remarks came as diplomatic efforts by Qatar continued to try to end a conflict that has destabilised the Middle East, disrupted shipping, driven up global energy prices and drawn in countries across the region.

The foreign minister said Iran’s red lines included keeping its highly enriched uranium in the country, though he said a “fair solution” was still possible.

He said Iran remains open to diplomacy with the United States but would not accept an agreement that compromises its dignity or undermines the victory it has achieved on the battlefield, IRNA reports.

Araghchi said Tehran was seeking a “good, honourable and dignified agreement,” stressing that any deal must safeguard Iran’s national interests and prevent a renewed conflict.

“We are seeking an agreement that would ensure there is no more war afterwards.”

US President Donald Trump’s envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner earlier met senior Qatari officials in Berlin on Thursday to discuss mediation efforts between the US and Iran, Axios reports according to Reuters, citing two sources with knowledge of the meeting.

Two tankers caught fire

Meanwhile, two tankers caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz, at the heart of the conflict between Iran and the US. “A tanker transiting outbound in the Strait of Hormuz has been hit on the stern by an unknown projectile. There are no reported casualties at this time,” the British maritime agency UKMTO stated.

Also, Iran said it shot down a US drone over Qeshm Island in the strait, according to Iranian state TV.

Araghchi has said reopening the Strait of Hormuz is “not difficult”, but requires the US to accept “reasonable conditions” under international law and acknowledge its “mistakes” and previous commitments, Al Jazeera reports.

articles.title: Textile exports rise 6.35pc in July-October
articles.summary:
ISLAMABAD: Pakistan’s textile and clothing exports grew by 6.35 per cent to $6.797 billion in July-October 2026–27, from $6.391bn in the corresponding period last year.

The modest rise in export proceeds was attributed to elevated input costs, which eroded exporters’ competitiveness, and external shocks that disrupted shipments, according to data from the Pakistan Bureau of Statistics.

The suspension of trade with Afghanistan since October 2025 and falling exports to the Middle East, especially the United Arab Emirates, due to the ongoing war in the region, were the key reasons for slow export growth.

High cost, war shocks and Afghan trade halt slow growth; oil import bill jumps on higher crude prices

The PBS data showed exports of readymade garments rose 13.91pc in value and 17.62pc in quantity during July-October FY27, while knitwear increased 3.97pc in value and 5.63pc in quantity. By contrast, bedwear dipped 0.70pc in value and 1.98pc in quantity.

Towel exports rose 10.06pc in value and 9.74pc in quantity in 4MFY27, whereas cotton cloth dipped 4.44pc in value and 6.06pc in quantity, respectively.

Yarn exports surged 30.17pc in 4MFY27. Exports of made-up articles, excluding towels, increased by 10.76pc, while tents, canvas, and tarpaulin fell by 34.07pc in 4MFY27.

Imports of synthetic fibre decreased by 14.40pc in 4MFY27, while the arrival of synthetic and artificial silk yarn rose by 9.06pc in 4MFY27. Imports of raw cotton increased 21.55pc in 4MFY27. However, arrival of second-hand clothes surged 22.52pc during the period year on year.

Rice exports

Negative growth was recorded in non-basmati rice exports in October in both quantity and value over the last year. Non-basmati exports dipped 3.27pc in value and 7.68pc in quantity in October on a year-on-year basis.

However, basmati exports grew 21.85pc in value and 18.39pc in quantity in October.

During the July-October period, exports of basmati rice surged 69.07pc and non-basmati by 27.03pc in value year on year. The increase was also noted in quantity for both basmati (64.79pc) and non-basmati (28.53pc), respectively.

The Ministry of Commerce has extended the subsidy scheme for rice exports by another three months until Sept 30 and raised the Duty Drawback of Local Taxes and Levies (DLTL) rate for non-basmati rice to support exporters facing weaker international demand.

Analysts linked the decline in non-basmati rice exports to the discontinuation of DLTL, as Pakistani rice is uncompetitive compared to Indian rice in the international market.

Oil imports

Pakistan’s oil import bill rose 9.34pc in 4MFY27 to $5.630bn from $5.149bn a year ago.

Data showed that crude oil imports increased by 33.07pc in value, with a decline of 8.37pc in quantity, indicating that the higher value is due to rising international oil prices. The value of petroleum products increased by 10.62pc, while quantity declined by 24.02pc in 4MFY27 year on year.

On the other hand, imports of liq­uefied natural gas declined by 47.19pc, while imports of liquefied petroleum gas grew by 18.88pc, ref­lecting demand for energy products.

Imports under the telecommunication group decreased by 7.30pc year on year, mainly due to a decline in other mobile phone imports in 4MFY27. Mobile handset imports declined by 7.20pc in the first four months of the current fiscal year compared with the same period last year.

articles.title: Nigeria, South Africa open reconciliation talks amid Fani-Kayode diplomatic row
articles.summary:
• Top officials hold closed-door meetings to ease tensions  •Tinubu reportedly intervenes   •Compensation for victims of xenophobic attacks remains uncertain

 

From Fred Itua and Aidoghie Paulinus, Abuja

Nigeria and South Africa have opened reconciliatory talks to strengthen diplomatic relations following the controversy involving Nigeria’s High Commissioner to Pretoria, Femi Fani-Kayode, amid concerns over recurring xenophobic attacks on Nigerians .

Daily Sun gathered that senior diplomatic officials from both countries have begun holding closed-door consultations to resolve outstanding differences and prevent the latest disagreement from undermining relations between Africa’s two major economies.

A diplomatic source, who spoke on condition of anonymity, confirmed that the two governments were already discussing ways to move beyond the controversy and strengthen bilateral cooperation.

“Yes, there are reconciliatory moves already. Both countries are already talking on ways that we can forge ahead,” the source said.

The renewed engagement comes against the backdrop of longstanding concerns over attacks on Nigerians and other foreign nationals in South Africa, which have resulted in loss of lives and property and heightened diplomatic tensions between Abuja and Pretoria.

According to information obtained by Daily Sun, more than 2,000 Nigerians have been evacuated from South Africa since June 10, 2026, through interventions involving the Federal Government and private organisations, including the Redeemed Christian Church of God.

However, it remains unclear whether the ongoing diplomatic discussions include compensation for Nigerians who lost relatives or property during the attacks.

Asked whether the issue had featured in the talks, the source said: “I can’t say if there will be any compensation.”

The reconciliatory moves also follow reports that President Bola Tinubu has initiated consultations with his South African counterpart, Cyril Ramaphosa, to ease tensions arising from Fani-Kayode’s recent confrontation with officials of the South African government.

Sources within the Presidential Villa and the Federal Ministry of Foreign Affairs claimed that Tinubu had reached out to Ramaphosa to reassure Pretoria of Nigeria’s commitment to maintaining cordial relations, although neither government has publicly confirmed such presidential communication.

The reported intervention came as consultations continued in Abuja over Fani-Kayode’s future following his formal reprimand by South Africa’s Department of International Relations and Cooperation (DIRCO) on November 17, four days after he presented his letters of credence to Ramaphosa.

Minister of Foreign Affairs was also said to have briefed the President on developments surrounding the dispute, while the Chief of Staff to the President, Femi Gbajabiamila, reportedly maintained contact with ministry officials as consultations continued.

The controversy began on November 13 when Fani-Kayode joined 14 other newly accredited ambassadors and high commissioners to present their credentials to Ramaphosa at the Sefako Makgatho Presidential Guest House in Pretoria.

Shortly after the ceremony, the Nigerian envoy alleged that his introduction and address had been deliberately excluded from the livestream of the event, unlike those of other diplomatic representatives.

He also claimed that he raised the matter with Ramaphosa during a photo session and that the South African President directed him to relevant officials.

The allegation drew a response from Ramaphosa’s spokesperson, Vincent Magwenya, who disputed Fani-Kayode’s account of the President’s involvement.

Magwenya maintained that Ramaphosa had neither directed the broadcaster nor interfered with its editorial operations but had merely referred the Nigerian envoy to an appropriate official to address his complaint.

Although the South African Presidency subsequently made footage of Fani-Kayode’s address available, the disagreement escalated into a public exchange involving the Nigerian High Commission and South African officials.

On November 17, DIRCO Director-General Zane Dangor summoned Fani-Kayode and formally conveyed Pretoria’s displeasure over his public comments and handling of the matter.

Dangor drew the envoy’s attention to Article 41 of the Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations, which requires diplomats to respect the laws and regulations of receiving states, refrain from interfering in their internal affairs and conduct official business through established diplomatic channels.

The South African government emphasised that official communications should pass through DIRCO, while reaffirming its commitment to maintaining constructive relations with Nigeria.

South Africa’s Minister of International Relations and Cooperation, Ronald Lamola, subsequently described the reprimand as a closed matter, indicating that Pretoria was prepared to move beyond the immediate disagreement while continuing to monitor developments.

Diplomatic sources told Daily Sun that the controversy could have been addressed through established diplomatic procedures without the public exchanges that followed.

They explained that complaints involving a host government were ordinarily handled through formal representations, diplomatic notes and other recognised channels rather than public statements capable of embarrassing either country.

A source familiar with the consultations said the manner in which the dispute unfolded had placed Nigeria in an uncomfortable diplomatic position.

“Whatever the merits of his complaint, the manner in which he handled it has put Nigeria in an awkward position with one of Africa’s biggest economies. A final decision on the recall is expected soon,” the source said.

Fani-Kayode, who was initially designated for Germany before his redeployment to South Africa, is also concurrently accredited to Lesotho and Eswatini.

His appointment came at a sensitive period in bilateral relations, following recurring tensions over xenophobic attacks, the treatment of Nigerian nationals and allegations of criminal activities involving some migrants.

In July, Lamola visited Abuja as Ramaphosa’s special envoy for discussions aimed at reducing tensions and strengthening diplomatic engagement.

Both governments subsequently emphasised the need to discourage inflammatory rhetoric, protect foreign nationals and address criminal conduct through lawful processes rather than collective blame or vigilante action.

At his November 13 accreditation ceremony, Fani-Kayode recalled Nigeria’s support for South Africa during the struggle against apartheid and pledged to strengthen cooperation between the countries.

Despite the subsequent controversy, the envoy and the Nigerian High Commission defended their position, while Fani-Kayode later described his meeting with Dangor as cordial and constructive.

Spokesperson of the Federal Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Femi Adeniyi, also declined to comment directly on the matter , maintaining that Fani-Kayode had been accredited and was performing his diplomatic responsibilities.

“Ambassador Femi Fani-Kayode has been accredited as Nigeria’s High Commissioner to South Africa. Therefore, he has since commenced the discharge of his diplomatic and representational duties, engaging with relevant South African authorities and key stakeholders on matters of mutual concern and shared interest to Nigeria and South Africa,” Adeniyi said.
