Leaders of the All Progressives Congress (APC) in the South East geopolitical zone have backed President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid in 2027 and expressed support for the party’s leadership in the region under the watch of Imo State Governor Hope Uzodimma.

The APC zonal leaders said that President Tinubu had done a lot for the zone to deserve re-election in the forthcoming presidential election, describing recent attacks on Governor Uzodimma as mischievous and aimed at frustrating Tinubu’s second tenure in office.

In a communiqué issued at the end of their zonal meeting, on Saturday, and signed by the Deputy National Chairman (South), Dr Benjamin Nwoye; National Treasurer, Chief Uguru Ofoke; and National Welfare Officer, Hon Donatus Nwankpa, among others, the APC stalwarts vowed to queue behind Uzodimma’s leadership of the party to actualise Tinubu’s re-election bid in 2027.

The communiqué read, “The South East Zonal Executives of the All Progressives Congress (APC), having thoroughly deliberated on matters of urgent political and organisational importance affecting the party in the zone, hereby issue this communiqué in firm and unambiguous response to the deliberate circulation of AI-generated images, fabricated statements, and other forms of fake news targeted at His Excellency, Distinguished Senator Hope Uzodimma, Executive Governor of Imo State and the Leader of the APC in the South East Zone.

“We note, with deep concern, the growing trend of digital mischief, character assassination, and coordinated misinformation campaigns designed to undermine the hard-earned political progress of the APC in the South East. These reckless publications seek not only to impugn the integrity of our Leader, but also to create artificial tension, sow seeds of distrust, and distract the party from its core mandate of delivering good governance and consolidating the Renewed Hope Agenda of President Bola Tinubu, GCFR.

“We reaffirm, without any reservation, whatsoever, our total, unalloyed, and unwavering support for, and absolute confidence in His Excellency, Distinguished Senator Hope Uzodimma, Executive Governor of Imo State and Leader of the All Progressives Congress in the South East Zone.

“We publicly acknowledge and deeply appreciate the consistent, substantial, and sacrificial support he has continued to extend to the party across the entire South East. This support has included significant financial contributions, logistical facilitation, strategic guidance, and personal mobilisation of party members and supporters, particularly during the recent Anambra Presidential Campaign Rally and other critical party programmes and activities throughout the zone. His leadership has remained a stabilising force and a major source of encouragement for APC structures in Abia, Anambra, Ebonyi, Enugu, and Imo States.”

It added, “We state categorically, emphatically, and for the avoidance of all doubt, that the publications currently in circulation, including AI-generated images, purported statements, insinuations, and related fake news materials, are entirely false, fabricated, and malicious. No such information, statements, opinions, or insinuations emanated from Senator Hope Uzodimma, nor can they be linked in any remote or indirect manner to his person, office, or authorised representatives. These materials are deliberate fabrications manufactured by faceless individuals and groups whose sole intention is to mislead the public, create unnecessary controversy, and manufacture political tension where none exists.

“We are fully aware, and we place it on record, that these publications are ill-conceived, carefully orchestrated, and deliberately intended to sow discord, generate artificial discontent, and create a false impression of friction between our major benefactor in the South East Zone and the Federal Government. This mischievous campaign is particularly reprehensible when viewed against the clear and consistent record of unwavering support that Senator Hope Uzodimma continues to give to the All Progressives Congress, the policies of the Federal Government, and the Renewed Hope Agenda of President Bola Tinubu in the South East. The authors of these materials seek to undermine the growing political harmony and progress that the APC is recording in the zone.”

The post 2027: South East APC leaders back Tinubu, Uzodimma appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

articles.title: 2027: Nigeria needs reset, not political insults –Makinde, APM
articles.summary:
From Ndubuisi Orji, Abuja and Oluseye Ojo, Ibadan

The presidential candidate of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM), Seyi Makinde, has declared that Nigeria needs a fundamental reset to overcome insecurity, poverty, hunger and infrastructural deficiencies, as his party challenged President Bola Tinubu to defend his administration’s record rather than resort to political insults ahead of the January 16, 2027 presidential election.

Makinde, who spoke in Abuja on Sunday, said Nigerians dissatisfied with the prevailing economic and security situation should embrace his Reset Nigeria Agenda, while urging citizens to pray for divine intervention in the country’s affairs rather than his personal victory at the polls.

His remarks coincided with a statement by the APM condemning Tinubu’s reported use of the Yoruba expression, “Egbe palemo,” at Saturday’s All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rally at Mapo Hall Arcade, Ibadan, which the opposition party interpreted as a disparaging reference to its political platform.

Speaking to journalists after attending a service at the headquarters of Dunamis International Gospel Centre, Makinde maintained that Nigeria was no longer providing the opportunities and benefits of governance that citizens deserved, insisting that a change in direction had become necessary.

“My message still is, if Nigeria is not working for you, then join me to press the reset button.

“Or if it’s working for you, okay, keep doing what you are doing, but I know Nigeria is not working,” he said.

The Oyo State governor explained that his presidential ambition was informed by the desire to restore public confidence in governance and recreate the opportunities that once enabled Nigerians to pursue their aspirations across the country.

He, however, maintained that the outcome of the election should ultimately reflect God’s will, stressing that his appeal for prayers was not intended to secure personal political advantage.

“When I came out to declare to run for president, what I asked people for was to pray that God should show mercy onto this country.

“I don’t even pray for me to be president of Nigeria, but pray that God’s will and God’s will alone be done.” Makinde said the spiritual dimension of national development could not be separated from the physical challenges confronting the country, urging Nigerians to remain committed to prayers while participating in efforts to improve governance.

“You can’t take this spiritual aspect away from the physical,” he said.

Makinde, who also attended a service at the Nongo u Kristu u i Ser u sha Tar (NKST), the Universal Reformed Christian Church, in Mabushi, Abuja, recalled his experience of moving from Oyo State to Rivers State as a young man in the 1990s before returning home and eventually becoming governor in 2019.

He cited the experience as an example of the opportunities he believed Nigeria should once again provide for its citizens.

Receiving him at the church, the resident pastor, Basil Orkpe, encouraged Makinde to remain committed to his presidential ambition, describing it as an opportunity to serve the country and alleviate the suffering of Nigerians.

“Without a shadow of a doubt, this great movement that God Himself has orchestrated has a purpose.

“Many people may have said, ‘Stop this, concentrate on something else’, but your heart’s desire and your cry to Jesus Christ have been that you would be able to serve this nation and, by extension, the rest of the world, and bring relief to the suffering of the people of this great land,” Orkpe said.

The cleric urged him not to be discouraged by opposition to his aspiration but to remain focused on what he described as the task of salvaging the country.

Meanwhile, the APM accused Tinubu of attempting to divert attention from the performance of his administration through political name-calling, arguing that Nigerians were more concerned about economic hardship, unemployment and insecurity than exchanges between rival political parties.

In a statement issued by the Director of Communication and spokesperson of the Oyo State APM Campaign Council, Yinka Oladoyinbo, the party said the President should explain what his administration had achieved since assuming office on May 29, 2023, rather than ridicule political opponents.

“We consider the expression a curious choice of words from a President whose administration has become synonymous with economic hardship, public frustration, political manoeuvring and an increasingly desperate search for electoral validation,” the statement said.

The party explained that the Yoruba word palemo could suggest hurriedly gathering or packing belongings, sometimes in preparation for departure, and questioned the President’s choice of expression.

“Mr President may wish to explain why such vocabulary comes so readily to him. As the saying goes, it takes a master of a craft to recognise the language of fellow practitioners. And when an accuser points one finger at another, the remaining four are invariably directed at himself,” it stated.

APM insisted that the challenges confronting Nigerians demanded concrete policy responses rather than political exchanges, maintaining that the rising cost of essential commodities, declining purchasing power and insecurity should dominate public debate ahead of the election.

“The APM will not be distracted by presidential name-calling. Nigerians are far more concerned about the cost of living, the purchasing power of their incomes, insecurity, unemployment, collapsing economic confidence and the daily struggle to survive than the linguistic theatrics of a campaign podium.

“A President seeking another mandate should be explaining what he has done with the first, not trading taunts with political opponents,” the party declared.

It further argued that Tinubu should have used his visit to Oyo State to address the economic difficulties confronting Nigerians and explain how his administration intended to improve living conditions.

The opposition party also rejected suggestions that the reception accorded Tinubu by the Olubadan of Ibadanland, Rashidi Ladoja, and the Soun of Ogbomoso, Ghandi Afolabi Olaoye, amounted to an endorsement of his re-election bid by the monarchs or their communities.

According to APM, traditional rulers are custodians of culture, history and communal harmony whose institutions should remain accessible to citizens irrespective of their political affiliations.

“A royal handshake does not constitute a ballot. A palace audience does not confer electoral authority. Political choreography cannot manufacture the consent of the people,” the statement said.

The party maintained that traditional institutions should preserve their neutrality and continue to provide platforms for dialogue, mediation and reconciliation rather than become instruments of partisan mobilisation.

“Their palaces must remain places where the ruling party, the opposition, the undecided and the politically disenchanted can find counsel, mediation and a sense of belonging. They are not campaign surrogates, electoral assets or instruments for manufacturing political legitimacy,” it added.

Invoking the Yoruba proverb, “Bi ikun lo ni oko, bi pakute, ipade d’ojo ibo,” APM maintained that neither presidential visits nor public appearances with traditional rulers could substitute for the freely expressed choices of voters.

It insisted that the January 16 presidential election would provide Nigerians an opportunity to assess the records and promises of the competing candidates and determine the country’s political direction.

The post 2027: Nigeria needs reset, not political insults –Makinde, APM appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

articles.title: Tinubu: Water stopped flowing while I was shaving in Villa
articles.summary:
• Admits electricity, water supply challenges, promises solutions

• Lagos must deliver maximum votes in 2027, says 200,000 out of 7m unacceptable

From Juliana Taiwo-Obalonye, Abuja

President Bola Tinubu has revealed that water supply was interrupted at the Presidential Villa in Abuja while he was shaving last Wednesday, acknowledging that the country’s electricity and water supply challenges persist even within the seat of power.

The President, who promised to address the infrastructure deficiencies, said his administration remained determined to improve essential services across the country, insisting that Nigeria had the capacity to overcome its development challenges.

Tinubu made the disclosure on Sunday at the Tinubu Family Special Prayer for his second-term re-election bid, held at the Yoruba Tennis Club, Onikan, Lagos, where he also challenged leaders of the All Progressives Congress (APC) to intensify voter mobilisation ahead of the January 16, 2027 presidential election.

Recalling his experience at the Villa, the President said the interruption demonstrated the inconvenience Nigerians faced because of inadequate public utilities.

“Last Wednesday, I was shaving when the water supply went off in the Villa o. You would not know the inconvenience that caused there, too.

“We will correct all these problems. No light, no water, no electricity, no development. We have only just started. We can do it, and we will do it for Nigeria,” he said.

Tinubu maintained that the difficulties confronting the country were surmountable, citing ongoing infrastructure development in Abuja and Lagos as evidence of what could be achieved through determination and sustained investment.

“There is nothing we cannot achieve. Look at Abuja; we have moved mountains. In Lagos, we have tamed the Atlantic. In Abuja, we have moved mountains to make way for development.

“There is nothing we cannot achieve if we put our hearts into it,” he declared.

Turning to preparations for the 2027 general election, the President expressed dissatisfaction with the level of voter mobilisation in Lagos, warning that the APC could not afford to record low turnout in a state with millions of registered voters.

He challenged party leaders and supporters to work towards securing the maximum possible votes for his re-election, arguing that winning with only a fraction of the state’s registered voters would fall short of expectations.

“To me, Lagos is the big deal. How can you have seven million registered voters and produce only 100,000 or 200,000? That is failure.

“Even if you win and say a win is a win, no. You have to generate the maximum number of votes,” Tinubu said.

He urged party members to set aside personal grievances, reconcile with aggrieved supporters and encourage eligible voters to obtain their Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs), stressing that internal disagreements should not undermine the party’s electoral preparations.

“It is not about anger. Anger will not do it. You may be angry with Silva or Mulika. Put that anger aside and call Mulika to go and vote.

“Call Mulika and let her go and vote. We finish the anger that day, and you can go back to it the next day. Do you get my message? We must generate enough votes to overwhelm them,” he said.

The President also directed his Special Adviser on Political Matters, Ibrahim Masari, to begin reconciliation efforts among aggrieved APC members, starting from Katsina State before extending the exercise to Jigawa and other parts of the country.

Describing Masari as his political confidant and bulldozer, Tinubu said the party needed to resolve internal differences and restore unity ahead of the election.

“To my confidant and bulldozer, Alhaji Masari, go back home and reconcile with everybody. That is the order of the President, and when you finish, move to Jigawa and other places and reconcile them, beg them. Badaru, you get what I said. We have to reconcile. Every anger must evaporate,” he declared.

Tinubu recalled his political disagreements in 2021 and 2022, saying he had to put aside personal grievances when former President Muhammadu Buhari invited him to serve as coordinator and co-chairman of the campaign.

He said political differences should not prevent party members from working together towards common objectives, urging them to embrace forgiveness and reconciliation.

“The first thing we ask from Allah is forgiveness. If you cannot give it, why are you asking Allah to forgive you? What you want from Him, you must be able to give to humanity,” he said.

The President also thanked members of the Tinubu family for their prayers and support throughout his political career, recalling their involvement during his governorship contests in Lagos and subsequent presidential ambition.

He said their continued encouragement had accompanied him through successive political challenges and campaigns.

Reflecting on the economic difficulties experienced during the 2022 and 2023 political transition, Tinubu recalled the cash scarcity and fuel shortages that affected Nigerians, maintaining that the challenges confronting the country today were less severe than those of the previous period.

“The challenges we face today are much easier than those of yesterday, but we must not take that for granted,” he said.

He also urged young Nigerians to prepare for leadership responsibilities, stressing that the task of building and sustaining the country would increasingly rest on their shoulders.

The event was attended by Lagos State Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu; Kwara State Governor AbdulRahman AbdulRazaq; Lateef Femi Okunnu; Chief of Staff to the President, Femi Gbajabiamila; and members of the Tinubu family, among other dignitaries.

The post Tinubu: Water stopped flowing while I was shaving in Villa appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

articles.title: Violence threatens election voter turnout, credibility of polls
articles.summary:
From Fred Itua, Romanus Ugwu, Okwe Obi, Abuja; Scholastica Hir, Makurdi; John Adams, Minna; Emmanuel Adeyemi, Lokoja; Jude Owuamanam, Jos

 

Attacks on campaign gatherings, destruction of political offices and billboards and alleged restrictions on opposition activities are heightening tension across the North Central, raising concerns about voter safety, participation and the credibility of the 2027 general elections.

Reports from Benue, Niger, Plateau, Kogi and the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) show that supporters of both the ruling and opposition parties have suffered attacks, while disputes over access to venues and political advertising are deepening accusations of an uneven campaign environment.

In Niger State, armed youths stormed the Trade Fair Complex in Minna after Governor Umaru Bago’s governorship campaign flag-off, hurling stones and sending supporters fleeing. Several people were injured, while police said six suspects were arrested with cutlasses, knives and scissors.

The incident followed an earlier attack in which the windscreens of three campaign vehicles belonging to the African Democratic Congress (ADC) were smashed.

Supporters of Bago and the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) governorship candidate, Mohammed Nami, also allegedly clashed in Lapai in October, leaving several people hospitalised.

In Benue, the PDP alleged that its billboards, including those of senatorial candidate Eunice Ortom, were destroyed, while its Benue Northeast senatorial candidate, Thomas Unongo, was harassed by suspected All Progressives Congress (APC) supporters on his way to a burial in Vandeikya.

The party’s secretary, Fan Nyikwagh, said political intolerance had extended to places of worship.

The ADC also complained that it was denied access to the Buruku Youth Centre and a secondary school for a stakeholders’ meeting.

Governor Hyacinth Alia and the police have appealed for restraint following the signing of a peace accord.

In Kogi, President Bola Tinubu’s campaign office in Lokoja was vandalised and posters pulled down, but almost a month after the incident, no arrest had been made.

The ADC separately alleged that thugs loyal to the APC attacked and set fire to its office in Dekina, threatening members of the party.

APC campaign spokesperson, Kingsley Fanwo, denied the party’s involvement in attacks on the opposition.

Kogi PDP Chairman, Mohammed Gambo, also accused the authorities of using political advertising charges to weaken opposition parties, citing a signage fee of N150 million for presidential candidates.

In Plateau, billboards and posters of Tinubu and Governor Caleb Mutfwang were pulled down before and after the North Central APC rally in Jos.

The APC attributed the destruction to disgruntled elements, insisting that the attacks did not amount to a rejection of the President by residents.

Police, however, said they had received no official complaint.

In the FCT, the Social Democratic Party (SDP) and Action Democratic Party (ADP) accused the ruling party of restricting the opposition’s access to the political space.

SDP spokesperson, Rufus Aiyenigba, alleged that parties were asked to pay as much as N250 million per billboard, describing the charges as an obstacle to political participation.

“This is not the democracy we laboured for,” he said.

The APC, however, accused sections of the opposition, particularly elements within the Obidient Movement, of promoting hostility towards Tinubu and his supporters.

Its National Youth Leader, Dayo Israel, cited the reported attack on the President’s convoy at a mosque in Abuja and warned that further attacks “will not be condoned”.

Security chiefs and political leaders have called for issue-based campaigns and warned against thuggery, while opposition parties are demanding action against attackers and access to public venues.

The post Violence threatens election voter turnout, credibility of polls appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

articles.title: Tinubu’s insistence on fuel subsidy removal insensitive –ADC
articles.summary:
From Ndubuisi Orji, Abuja

The African Democratic Congress Presidential Campaign Council (ADC-PCC) has criticised President Bola Tinubu’s insistence on sustaining the removal of fuel subsidy, describing his position as insensitive to millions of Nigerians still grappling with rising living costs, hunger and poverty.

The campaign council said the President’s remarks at the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rally in Ibadan at the weekend suggested that his administration was unwilling to acknowledge the hardship which, it argued, had followed the implementation of its economic policies.

In a statement issued yesterday by its Director of Media and Publicity, Kola Ologbondiyan, the ADC-PCC accused Tinubu of displaying a lack of empathy for Nigerians whose purchasing power had been eroded by rising prices of food, transportation and other essential commodities.

It questioned the President’s reported suggestion that Nigerians should put the subsidy removal controversy behind them, arguing that the consequences of the policy remained evident in the daily struggles of households across the country.

“The President appears more interested in being addressed as Mr President than in tackling the crushing realities confronting the people. That explains his brash insistence that Nigerians should forget about fuel subsidy removal simply because, in his estimation, it belongs to the past.

“How can hardship, hunger and widespread poverty, which are direct consequences of the hurriedly imposed economic policies of the Tinubu administration, suddenly become things of the past when Nigerians continue to bear their devastating consequences every day?

“To ask Nigerians to forget a policy whose consequences they confront every waking moment is not only insensitive; it is an insult to their intelligence and a mockery of their suffering,” the council stated.

The opposition campaign council maintained that the administration’s continued defence of its economic reforms, despite complaints over their impact on household incomes, raised questions about its willingness to review policies that had imposed additional burdens on citizens.

It argued that responsible leadership required listening to public concerns, acknowledging shortcomings in policy implementation and making adjustments where necessary to alleviate hardship.

According to the council, the government’s approach had been characterised by a determination to defend its decisions rather than address the immediate difficulties confronting Nigerians.

The ADC-PCC further warned against allowing the debate over the administration’s economic policies to overshadow what it described as concerns about the state of democratic institutions and the welfare of citizens.

“Nigeria cannot afford a second term built on the ruins of its democratic institutions and the continued impoverishment of its citizens.

“Nigerians deserve a government that feels their pain, understands their struggles and takes deliberate steps to ease their burden, not one that dismisses their suffering or asks them to forget the circumstances that have made life increasingly unbearable.”

The campaign council maintained that the January 16, 2027 presidential election would provide Nigerians an opportunity to assess the administration’s performance and determine the country’s political direction.

“In 2027, Nigerians will have the opportunity to change this narrative. The power to rescue the country and restore hope rests firmly in their hands,” the statement added.

The post Tinubu’s insistence on fuel subsidy removal insensitive –ADC appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

articles.title: Borno youths develop affordable local foods to tackle child malnutrition
articles.summary:
From Timothy Olanrewaju, Maiduguri

Young innovators in Borno State have developed locally produced, ready-to-use nutritious foods aimed at combating child malnutrition, offering a potentially affordable and accessible alternative for vulnerable children suffering from nutritional deficiencies.

The food products, made from locally sourced ingredients, were unveiled at a youth-led nutrition challenge organised by the United Nations Children’s Fund (UNICEF) in Maiduguri at the weekend to commemorate the 2026 World Children’s Day.

Health experts at the event described the innovations as nutritious and affordable, while UNICEF said the initiative demonstrated the potential of young people to develop practical solutions to malnutrition using resources available within their communities.

UNICEF Chief of Maiduguri Field Office, Francis Butichi, said the competition was designed not only to address acute malnutrition but also to encourage young people to collaborate, innovate and contribute directly to improving child nutrition.

“The youth-led nutrition challenge is more than an effort to address acute malnutrition. It is a platform for young people to collaborate and create local solutions to a global problem.”

Butichi explained that the participants sourced nutritious ingredients locally to develop food products that could be affordable and accessible to children affected by malnutrition, particularly in vulnerable communities.

He said the initiative reflected UNICEF’s commitment to supporting homegrown innovations capable of improving children’s health and wellbeing.

According to him, the commemoration of World Children’s Day provided an opportunity to celebrate children while renewing commitments to their rights, survival, development and protection from preventable illnesses.

He stressed that every child deserved the opportunity to grow up healthy and fulfil their potential, adding that tackling acute malnutrition remained essential to achieving that objective.

“We urge our young people to keep going. The world is waiting for your creative ideas for the nutrition of children right here in Borno. UNICEF will continue to support you,” Butichi said.

Director of Community and Family Health at the Borno State Primary Health Care Development Board, Abdulwahab Mala, commended UNICEF for its interventions in child health and nutrition across Borno, Adamawa and Yobe states.

Mala, who represented the Borno State Government at the event, said the state recognised the progress recorded in efforts to prevent and manage malnutrition, describing the youth-led initiative as a demonstration of collective commitment to improving child health.

“Malnutrition is a scourge and it is possible to deal with it. This collective initiative is a reflection of our bold commitment to child health,” he said.

He also commended the state government for expanding access to healthcare services across several local government areas, maintaining that improved healthcare delivery and collaborative interventions were essential to addressing the nutritional needs of vulnerable children.

The post Borno youths develop affordable local foods to tackle child malnutrition appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

articles.title: Tinubu commits N450bn to agricultural financing, targets 2m farmers –APC
articles.summary:
The All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council has said President Bola Tinubu’s administration has committed N450 billion to agricultural financing programmes aimed at boosting domestic food production, improving food security and expanding access to credit for smallholder farmers across the country.

The council also disclosed that the President had approved a N1.5 trillion recapitalisation of the Bank of Agriculture (BOA) to strengthen its capacity to provide affordable financing to farmers, cooperatives, processors and other operators in the agricultural value chain.

In a statement issued by its spokesperson, Dele Alake, the campaign council said more than 500,000 smallholder farmers across 16 states, including over 70,000 women, had benefited from agricultural interventions under the Renewed Hope Agenda, while the government was targeting two million farmers through an expanded support programme.

According to the council, the N450 billion intervention comprises the N250 billion Renewed Hope Smallholder Support and Value Chain Fund and the N200 billion Guaranteed Minimum Price Programme, designed to address farmers’ financing challenges, improve access to agricultural inputs and reduce losses arising from unstable commodity prices.

It explained that the N250 billion fund was being implemented through Farmer Aggregation Companies responsible for coordinating farmer registration, input distribution, extension services and market linkages.

The programme, it said, had facilitated the distribution of approximately 2.5 million bags of fertiliser and 300,000 bags of certified seeds, with plans to expand coverage to two million farmers and distribute more than 10 million bags of fertiliser.

The council maintained that the interventions were particularly important in Northern Nigeria, where agriculture remained a major source of employment and household income.

It listed Kaduna, Kano, Katsina, Niger, Borno, Gombe, Taraba, Adamawa, Yobe and Bauchi among states receiving attention under the agricultural financing programmes.

On efforts to protect farmers against price fluctuations and distress sales, the campaign council said the Bank of Agriculture was implementing the N200 billion Guaranteed Minimum Price Programme, under which approximately 170,000 metric tonnes of maize, rice, sorghum and cassava had been procured.

It explained that the initiative was intended to strengthen agricultural commodity markets and provide farmers with greater certainty over returns on their produce.

The council also highlighted a financing arrangement for onion farmers, developed by the Bank of Agriculture in partnership with the National Onion Producers, Processors and Marketers Association of Nigeria (NOPPMAN), representing more than 11,800 farmers.

Under the Onion Financing Programme, farmers are expected to receive support for improved seeds and fertiliser, while processors would have access to commodity purchase financing and facilities for storage and solar-powered cooling to reduce post-harvest losses.

The arrangement requires participating cooperatives to contribute 30 per cent of their input costs, with the Bank of Agriculture financing the remaining 70 per cent.

On the proposed N1.5 trillion recapitalisation, the APC campaign council said the intervention would strengthen the bank’s financial position and enable it to expand lending to underserved farming communities, agricultural cooperatives, processors and commercial producers.

It described the recapitalisation as part of Tinubu’s commitment to strengthening agricultural financing and transforming the sector into a major contributor to economic growth and employment.

The council further disclosed that the bank was working with the All Farmers Association of Nigeria on a dry-season financing programme targeting 400,000 farmers during the 2026 farming cycle.

The initiative covers a proposed 120,000 hectares of wheat cultivation and another 300,000 hectares for rice, maize, sorghum, millet, cassava and soybeans.

It also cited the Nigeria Ginger Recovery Programme, which it said had supported 3,200 farmers in Kachia, Kaduna State, with blight-free seeds and recovered more than 9,000 bags for multiplication, with plans to extend the intervention to 20,000 hectares across 16 states.

For women farmers, the council said the Bank of Agriculture was targeting at least 50,000 beneficiaries through insured cooperative production financing at an interest rate of nine per cent, in collaboration with the Federal Ministries of Women Affairs and Agriculture.

The statement also disclosed that 1,571 tractors had been deployed to 23 states under the Renewed Hope National Agricultural Mechanisation Programme, with a target of mechanising 1.2 million hectares of farmland through qualified mechanisation service providers.

Other interventions highlighted included a N385 billion productive-use-of-electricity programme involving 44,000 electric cargo tricycles and 100,000 solar irrigation pumps, intended to support approximately 500,000 farming families.

The campaign council maintained that the combined interventions demonstrated the administration’s commitment to addressing agricultural financing constraints, increasing domestic production and strengthening food security.

It said expanding access to credit, improved seeds, fertiliser, mechanisation, irrigation and reliable commodity markets would help farmers increase productivity and improve their incomes.

The post Tinubu commits N450bn to agricultural financing, targets 2m farmers –APC appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

articles.title: Enugu police launch manhunt for fleeing kidnappers
articles.summary:
The Commissioner for Police in Enugu State, Fidelis Ogarabe, has ordered a manhunt for the fleeing kidnappers of a 73-year-old man, Patrick Onyia.

Mr Onyia ‌‌‍‌‌‌regained his freedom last Thursday, following sustained rescue operations by the police, in collaboration with Forest Guards and the Neighbourhood Watch personnel.

Spokesman of the Enugu State Police Command, Daniel Ndukwe,  said the directive was issued on Friday. He said that the victim was abducted at about 6pm last Wednesday, in the Umuabi community, Udi Local Council.

“Preliminary investigations revealed that the abductors allegedly used the victim’s ATM card to withdraw an unspecified sum of money from his bank account before fleeing.

“The commissioner directed operatives to intensify efforts to track down and arrest the perpetrators and bring them to justice,” he said.

The police chief reassured residents of the command’s commitment to protecting life and property.

Ndukwe said the commissioner urged members of the public to provide credible information that could help apprehend the fleeing suspects.

The post Enugu police launch manhunt for fleeing kidnappers appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

articles.title: NDC condemns 200-man vigilante in Ebonyi LG, urges investigation
articles.summary:
From Uchenna Inya, Abakaliki

The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) in Ebonyi State has condemned the reported establishment and inauguration of a 200-member local security codenamed Neighbourhood Watch outfit by the Chairman, Ohaozara Local Government Area, Osborn Nweze Umahi.

Umahi inaugurated the 200-man vigilante at the weekend in Obiozara, headquarters of the local government.

NDC wondered why the action occurred at the critical period when the state was  approaching another electoral season.

In a statement signed by the state Chairman of the party, Alum Enyinnaya Udensi and the state Secretary, Okereke Nnanna, the party said that while it  recognises the legitimate responsibility of government to protect life and property, the party is deeply concerned about the timing, circumstances, composition, and possible implications of establishing such a large security outfit barely months before a general election.

“We find it particularly disturbing that a party that has had the opportunity to serve the people for the past 11 years, yet has failed to substantially improve the living conditions, economic fortunes and general welfare of the citizens, is suddenly demonstrating such urgency in establishing a 200-man security structure at a politically sensitive period.

“The question that begs for an answer is: What is the real intention behind this sudden mobilisation of 200 security personnel, and whose interests are they expected to protect?”, the party queried.

The party stated that if the initiative was genuinely intended to strengthen community security, the government must demonstrate transparency by making public the legal framework guiding its operations, the nature of equipment to be deployed, its chain of command, training arrangements, and the mechanisms for ensuring accountability.

It  noted that the party was  particularly concerned by any possibility that an ostensibly community-based security arrangement could be transformed into an instrument of political intimidation, harassment, voter suppression, or electoral violence.

“Let it be clearly understood that the security of our communities must never be converted into a political project or a weapon for intimidating political opponents and innocent citizens.

“Our warning is unequivocal: Whoever stokes violence, promotes intimidation or attempts to manipulate the electoral process through coercion will ultimately be consumed by the consequences of such actions.

“No individual, political office holder, or group should mistake the peaceful disposition of the people for weakness. We wish to remind those in positions of authority that the mandate given to them is an opportunity to improve the lives of ordinary Ebonyi people, provide employment, strengthen infrastructure, improve healthcare, support education, and create an environment where citizens can live with dignity and security.

“Unfortunately, the people are still confronted with enormous developmental challenges”.

The party maintained that it is unacceptable that the urgency now being demonstrated in establishing a massive security structure is not matched by the same level of commitment to addressing unemployment, poverty, insecurity, and the numerous hardships confronting our people.

“The NDC further wishes to remind the authorities of an important African proverb: “Whosoever harvests an ant-infested firewood has invited the lizards to a feast.”

“Those who create conditions for political tension, intimidation, and insecurity should not be surprised when the consequences become difficult to contain. Those who sow violence must understand that its consequences may extend far beyond their immediate expectations.

The party called on the Nigeria Police Force and other relevant security institutions to urgently investigate the development.

“Specifically, we demand that the security agencies establish the legality of the newly inaugurated 200-member outfit and ascertain the legal authority for possessing and deploying such arms.

“Investigate the recruitment process, training, operational guidelines, and actual mandate of the outfit. Ensure that no member of the outfit is deployed to intimidate political opponents, interfere with political activities or influence the choices of voters.

The party also urged the security agencies to put adequate safeguards in place to prevent the misuse of public resources and security structures during the forthcoming elections.

“We emphasise that the responsibility for maintaining law and order rests with constitutionally recognised security institutions. Community-based security arrangements must operate strictly within the law and under appropriate supervision”, the party said.

The party noted that it will not fold its arms while any development capable of undermining the peace, safety, and democratic rights of our people goes unquestioned. The party also called on the people of Ohaozara and, indeed, all Ebonyi citizens to remain calm, vigilant, and law-abiding, and also urge their supporters and members to resist provocation and conduct themselves peacefully while exercising their democratic rights.

“Finally, we remind the security agencies that their constitutional responsibility is to protect the lives and properties of all citizens, irrespective of political affiliation. They must live up to their expectations before, during, and after the elections.

“Ebonyi State belongs to all of us, and its security must never be sacrificed on the altar of political ambition. Our democracy must be protected, our people must be free, and the will of the electorate must prevail.

articles.title: Analysis-Can climate diplomacy build on the collapse of COP31?
articles.summary:
By Peter Hobson, Simon Jessop, Valerie Volcovici and Sarah McFarlane

ANTALYA, Turkey, Nov 23 (Reuters) - The collapse of COP31 talks in Turkey on Sunday without a political agreement left exhausted negotiators questioning the future of a process that for three decades has led the global fight against climate change.

For the small, vulnerable countries most exposed to rising sea levels and the increasingly extreme weather scientists link to rising carbon emissions, annual UN conferences are their chance to draw the world's attention to their plight and seek financial help.

articles.title: Iran strike wounds two in Bahrain, Saudi condemns 'criminal' attacks
articles.summary:
Bahrain said Sunday that two people were wounded in an Iranian strike the previous day on "a civilian industrial site" in the Gulf kingdom, which has faced several attacks this week.

Iran's Revolutionary Guards have repeatedly said they targeted US facilities in Bahrain, where Iranian strikes resumed on November 13 after a lull since early September.

"In the wake of the criminal Iranian attacks suffered yesterday (Saturday) by the Kingdom of Bahrain... a Bahraini national with a disability was wounded," Bahrain's interior ministry said on X.

articles.title: Libya's eastern government suspects drone attack caused explosion on Russian ship
articles.summary:
By Ayman Al-Warfali

Nov 22 (Reuters) - A suspected drone attack caused an explosion aboard a Russian ship docked at the Benghazi naval base in eastern Libya, the country's eastern-based government said on Sunday after a preliminary investigation.

No one has claimed responsibility for the suspected attack, and there was no immediate reaction from Russian authorities.

Since Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, Ukrainian forces have repeatedly used naval drones and missiles to target Russian warships and naval facilities, mainly in the Black Sea.

articles.title: Drone strikes hit homes, UN building in Sudan's capital
articles.summary:
Drones struck Sudan's capital Khartoum, damaging residential homes and a United Nations building on Sunday, witnesses and the world organisation said.

Explosions were heard in the area around Khartoum airport and other parts of the city from around 2:00 am until approximately 4:30 am.

A drone strike completely destroyed a house, a witness said, while a Sudanese army source said the drones had been launched from Ethiopia.

articles.title: Netanyahu, Eisenkot parties end talks without deal on forming Israel govt
articles.summary:
The parties of caretaker Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his rival Gadi Eisenkot concluded a new round of talks on Sunday without reaching an agreement on a possible coalition government, which would require concessions from both sides.

Delegations from Eisenkot's Yashar party and Netanyahu's Likud met for four hours at a hotel in Herzliya, near Tel Aviv, following a first round of discussions last Sunday.

articles.title: COP31 climate talks set to collapse without political deal
articles.summary:
ANTALYA, Turkey, Nov 22 (Reuters) - UN climate talks in Turkey looked set to collapse without a political agreement after COP31 summit president Murat Kurum said there would be no new draft of the deal.

Earlier, multiple countries and negotiating blocs said they could not accept the version of the text put before them.

"There will be no new text from now on. We will not be carrying out work on a new text in an environment where there is no consensus," Kurum said.

(Reporting by Tuvan Gumrukcu, writing by William James)

articles.title: Israel's Eisenkot condemns arson attacks by Jewish settlers in West Bank
articles.summary:
By Ali Sawafta and Mohammed Torokman

RAMALLAH, Nov 22 (Reuters) - Israeli militant settlers attacked Palestinian villages in the occupied West Bank early on Sunday, starting fires and scrawling racist graffiti, residents said, prompting an accusation of "Jewish terrorism" from the man trying to form an Israeli government.

articles.title: Climate deal collapses in chaotic end to COP31
articles.summary:
The COP31 climate talks ended in failure Sunday as a contentious deal collapsed over fossil fuels and the summit in Turkey stretched into record overtime.

The final agreement was rejected in a chaotic finale to a UN climate summit that ran two days over schedule, underscoring the strains on diplomacy in an increasingly fractured world.

UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres, who urged nations to send fossil fuels "the way of the dinosaurs" during a fiery appearance at the talks, expressed deep dismay.

articles.title: Bahrain says Iran strikes industrial facility as air defences intercept attacks
articles.summary:
Nov 21 (Reuters) - Bahrain said an Iranian attack hit a civilian industrial facility on Saturday, while Iran's Revolutionary Guards said they had launched a missile-and-drone assault on US military positions in the kingdom, home to the US Navy's Fifth Fleet.

In a statement on Sunday, Bahrain's Interior Ministry said two people were injured in Iranian attacks on the country during the previous day - a Pakistani resident, who was in a critical condition, and a Bahraini citizen, who was stable.

articles.title: Countries react as COP31 climate talks collapse
articles.summary:
ANTALYA, Turkey, Nov 22 (Reuters) - The COP31 conference in Turkey ended in collapse on Sunday after countries failed to agree an overarching political deal on how to tackle climate change.

Below are reactions from delegates:

ANTONIO GUTERRES, UNITED NATIONS SECRETARY GENERAL

"I am deeply disappointed that COP31 has ended without consensus on an overarching outcome. I share the very profound frustration of all those who expected governments to rise to the moment the climate crisis demands."

articles.title: Bahrain says Iran struck industrial site as tankers hit in Hormuz
articles.summary:
Bahrain accused Iran of striking a civilian industrial facility on Saturday, causing a fire and damage but no casualties, while two tankers were hit in the Strait of Hormuz, at the heart of the Middle East conflict.

The Gulf kingdom has suffered several attacks this week, ending a weeks-long lull in the conflict that began with US-Israeli strikes on Iran in late February.

articles.title: In an Egypt village, generations of Palestinians denied a normal life
articles.summary:
Shamma Abu Hussein is possibly the last person in her village of refugees to have lived in historic Palestine. Living in Egypt, she has watched three generations of her family grow up in legal limbo.

She was among the hundreds of thousands who fled or were expelled during the creation of the State of Israel in 1948, whose descendants number in the millions.

Now she fears that the effects of the Gaza war and rhetoric from Israeli ministers calling for Gazans to be expelled means history is repeating itself.

articles.title: Syrian Christian town demands security after resident kidnapped
articles.summary:
When Amina saw her nephew's motorbike knocked onto the ground and a car speeding away from his home in central Syria, she thought there had been a crash.

Instead, 38-year-old jeweller Maher Sankari had been kidnapped, an incident that plunged the Christian town of Suqaylabiyah into fear and prompted church leaders to demand authorities take action against repeated attacks and kidnappings of Christians.

Sankari's captors are demanding an eye-watering ransom of 120 kilogrammes (265 pounds) of gold.

articles.title: COP31 climate talks collapse as EU and others reject deal
articles.summary:
By Peter Hobson, Lewis Jackson and Ezgi Erkoyun

ANTALYA, Turkey, Nov 22 (Reuters) - UN climate talks ended in collapse on Sunday as the European Union and others rejected a final deal put forward by COP31 presidents Turkey and Australia, saying it was too weak to advance the fight against global warming.

The failed talks reflect the struggle by governments across the world to muster ambitious action to address the worsening consequences of climate change — including heatwaves, wildfires, floods and powerful storms — as wars and economic pressures compete for their attention.

articles.title: US denies Iranian account that missile damaged F-16 over Gulf
articles.summary:
Nov 21 (Reuters) - US Central Command on Saturday denied an Iranian account that its forces had fired a missile at a US F-16 fighter jet over the Gulf, damaging the aircraft and forcing it to make an emergency landing.

Iranian state media earlier reported that the country's air defence systems targeted the aircraft on Friday evening, causing it to abort its mission and land at a nearby airport.

articles.title: UK man swims in Strait of Hormuz to highlight environmental damage
articles.summary:

"Oil tankers, gas carriers and other merchant ships are being attacked, day after day. The environmental consequences of this war will last for generations," Lewis Pugh wrote in a post on his website.

articles.title: Israeli strike on vehicle in Gaza kills three, Gaza Health Ministry says
articles.summary:
JERUSALEM, Nov 21 (Reuters) - Israeli forces hit a truck in Gaza on Saturday which witnesses said was carrying food and papers bearing the logo of the World Central Kitchen charity, but the organisation said the vehicle was not affiliated with it.

The Gaza Health Ministry said three people were killed in the incident in Gaza City.

The Israeli military said its forces had been targeting Islamic Jihad militants in the area at the time and that the vehicle had been transporting food to members of the organisation.

articles.title: COP31 climate summit risks failure as talks go deep into overtime
articles.summary:
By Valerie Volcovici and Sarah McFarlane

ANTALYA, Turkey, Nov 21 (Reuters) - The COP31 climate summit will either produce a good deal or no deal at all, the European Union's top climate official said on Saturday as talks stretched deep into overtime.

Negotiators from nearly 200 countries are struggling to bridge divisions over fossil fuels and climate finance, delaying an agreement at the two-week conference that had been scheduled to end on Friday.

articles.title: Gaza civil defence says Israeli fire kills four
articles.summary:
Gaza's civil defence told AFP that Israeli fire killed four people on Saturday, including three in a strike on a vehicle carrying food aid in the war-ravaged territory.

The Israeli military said it had struck "three terrorists from the military wing" of Islamic Jihad who had been travelling in a van carrying food and supplies for the militant group allied with Hamas.

articles.title: Fire at power station in Iraq's Basra kills at least 4, injures 35
articles.summary:
BASRA, Iraq, Nov 21 (Reuters) - At least 4 people were killed and 35 injured in a fire at a power station in southern Iraq on Saturday, with the toll expected to rise, security officials said.

Civil defence teams brought the fire at the Hartha power station north of Basra under control after firefighters responded to the incident, Iraq's state news agency, INA, reported.

The fire spread to neighbouring houses and forced operations at the power station to stop, the security officials said.

Child rescued alive from under the rubble in Dymer
articles.summary:
Rescuers have recovered a third body and pulled a child alive from beneath the rubble of a residential building in Dymer, Kyiv Oblast.

Source: Tymur Tkachenko, Head of Kyiv Oblast Military Administration

Quote: "Rescue workers have recovered the body of a third victim from beneath the rubble of a residential building in Dymer."

Update: At 18:55, Tkachenko reported that during search and rescue operations in Dymer, rescue workers pulled a child out alive.

Background:

It had previously been reported that two people had been killed and four injured as a result of the Russian attack. One of those killed was an 18-year-old man.

Rescue workers were searching for 11 people, including two children.

President Volodymyr Zelenskyy previously reported that a section of a five-storey apartment building in Dymer had been partially destroyed in a Russian drone strike. Nine people were evacuated, and 14 others were unaccounted for.

articles.title: Three people killed and fifteen injured in strike on shop in Vyshneve
articles.summary:
The death toll from a Russian strike on a grocery store in Vyshneve in Kyiv Oblast has risen to three, with 15 people injured.

Source: President Volodymyr Zelenskyy in his evening address; Vyshneve Mayor Illia Dikov

Quote from Zelenskyy: "There was also a strike in Vyshneve, Kyiv Oblast today – against an ordinary grocery store. Three people were killed and 13 injured."

Details: Zelenskyy also reported that the child rescued from beneath the rubble in Dymer in Kyiv Oblast is a boy. He is receiving medical treatment.

Quote from Zelenskyy: "Unfortunately, there is still no information about ten people. As of now, we know that four people have been killed… A Russian Shahed struck this building, practically blowing a section of it to smithereens. Rescue efforts are complicated by constant new air raid alerts and renewed threats. There are sufficient rescue personnel and resources at the scene – more than 130 people are involved. The operation in Dymer will continue until we have complete information about every single person."

The site of the attack in Vyshneve
Photo: Illia Dikov

Update: Dikov reports that three people were killed and 15 injured as a result of the Russian strike, including three children.

Quote from Dikov: "A Shahed crashed on the Novus supermarket in the town of Vyshneve. The roof and the shop premises have been damaged."

Background:

In Vyshneve in the Bucha district of Kyiv Oblast, a shop building was damaged as a result of a Russian attack, with two people reported killed and eight injured.

In Dymer in Kyiv Oblast, rescue workers recovered a third body and pulled a child alive from beneath the rubble of a residential building.

As a result of a Russian drone strike in Dymer, the entrance section of a five-storey building was severely damaged.

articles.title: Woman killed and nine injured in Russian attacks on Dnipropetrovsk Oblast
articles.summary:
One person has been killed and another nine injured as a result of Russian attacks on Dnipropetrovsk Oblast on 22 November.

Source: Oleksandr Hanzha, Head of Dnipropetrovsk Oblast Military Administration

Quote: "One person has been killed and nine injured. The enemy attacked five districts more than 40 times with drones, artillery and aerial bombs."

Details: In the city of Dnipro, residential buildings and infrastructure have been damaged. A woman has been killed. A 22-year-old man is in a serious condition and a 49-year-old man is in a moderate condition. The Russians also struck energy infrastructure.

In the Dnipro district, the Russians targeted infrastructure.

In the Nikopol district, the city of Nikopol, as well as the Marhanets, Chervonohryhorivka, and Pokrovske hromadas, came under attack. A 64-year-old man is in a serious condition, a 65-year-old woman was taken to hospital in a moderate condition and a 55-year-old man is being treated at home. [A hromada is an administrative unit designating a village, several villages, or a town, and their adjacent territories.]

In the Synelnykove district, the Russians targeted the Pokrovske, Mykolaivka, and Petropavlivka hromadas. A shop, cars and infrastructure were damaged. A 63-year-old man is in a serious condition and one person is receiving outpatient treatment.

In the Kamianske district, infrastructure was damaged. Two men aged 51 and 62 are in hospital in a moderate condition.

articles.title: Czech PM opposes funding for Ukraine through the EU budget
articles.summary:
Czech Prime Minister Andrej Babiš has said that the current draft budget for the European Union is completely unacceptable to his country, particularly because it includes support for Ukraine.

Source: České noviny, citing Babiš in a video on X (Twitter), as reported by European Pravda

Details: Babiš criticised cuts to funding for Czechia and spending on the European Parliament and other EU institutions, as well as on support for Ukraine, which is in its fifth year of defending itself against Russian military aggression.

On Saturday 21 November, European Council President António Costa presented a revised negotiating framework for the EU's future seven-year budget for 2028-2034. It provides for a cut of €204 billion compared to the plan initially presented by the European Commission, which some countries consider too onerous.

Babiš, for his part, has criticised the cuts to budget expenditure. According to Babiš, the Irish Presidency is proposing cutting the budget by €32 billion.

"This is completely unacceptable to us," he said.

The Irish Presidency, mentioned by the Czech PM, submitted a budget proposal back in October, whereas the proposal presented on Saturday comes from European Council President Costa. According to Babiš, Czechia is contributing increasingly more funds to the EU budget.

"Now, under the Irish Presidency's proposal, they are even going to cut CZK 7.5 billion [about US$336.33 million] from us," he added.

Babiš criticised the fact that, according to the draft EU budget, European institutions will cost €100 billion over seven years. He refused to allocate €100 billion from the budget for aid to Ukraine.

"Why should we give money from the European budget to Ukraine? Ukraine should receive money from outside the European budget," Babiš said.

Foreign Minister Petr Macinka fully agrees with Babiš's assessment of the EU budget proposal, as he told journalists at Prague Airport. According to Macinka, the negotiations are not easy.

"It is certainly important to voice comments, observations or even disagreement, because that is precisely how a final agreement is reached," he noted.

Macinka believes that Czechia's position will have a positive influence on the final shape of the budget.

"The debate regarding financial aid to Ukraine is undoubtedly justified and relevant, but it is a different discussion, and it must be kept separate from the debate regarding the EU budget," Macinka added.

Czechia is still a net recipient of the EU budget, but according to analysts, as its prosperity grows, the situation may change in the coming years. Last year, the Czech Republic received CZK 31.1 billion (US$1.39 billion) more from the EU budget than it contributed, as the Ministry of Finance previously reported.

Background:

On 21 November, António Costa presented his own proposal for the European Union's multiannual budget for 2028-2034. The proposal envisages a reduction in overall spending compared with the European Commission's initial proposal but maintains up to €100 billion in funding for Ukraine at current price levels.

The day before, Austria stated that European Council President António Costa must make radical cuts to the EU's long-term budget for Vienna to agree to it.

articles.title: Emergency power outages in effect in five Ukrainian oblasts
articles.summary:
Emergency power outages are in effect in Dnipropetrovsk, Kharkiv, Poltava, Zaporizhzhia, and Sumy oblasts as of the evening of 22 November.

Source: Ukrenergo, Ukraine's state-owned electricity transmission operator

Quote: "Russia has once again attacked energy infrastructure in Dnipropetrovsk Oblast. The strike has caused damage to equipment, which has affected the stability of the power supply in the oblast.

As of now, emergency power outages are being implemented in Dnipropetrovsk, Kharkiv, Poltava, Zaporizhzhia and Sumy oblasts."

Details: Ukrenergo noted that repair crews will begin dealing with the aftermath of the attack as soon as the security situation permits.

Meanwhile, in Odesa Oblast, work is ongoing to repair the electricity transmission network that was significantly damaged as a result of Russian attacks. Repair crews are working around the clock to restore the power supply to Odesa and the surrounding districts. The repairs require complex technical solutions and a substantial amount of work.

articles.title: Poland flags Russian disinformation over alleged Ukrainian attack in Kaliningrad Oblast
articles.summary:
Numerous fake Russian disinformation messages surrounding reports of an alleged Ukrainian attack on Kaliningrad Oblast are being recorded in Poland.

Source: Polish radio station RMF24, as reported by European Pravda

Details: Poland's Centre for Countering Disinformation is closely monitoring the media and social media, Deputy Minister of Digital Affairs Paweł Olszewski announced on 22 November.

Olszewski cited examples of the disinformation messages. Among them, in particular, were reports claiming that: "German troops stationed in Poland are coordinating a Ukrainian attack on Królewiec Oblast [the Polish name for Kaliningrad Oblast]", as well as "Lithuanians and Poles are attacking Russia using Ukrainian missiles".

Olszewski also cited examples of false reports claiming that "Ukrainians are attacking Russia to drag Poland into the war", and that "NATO has attacked Kaliningrad".

"Remember to check reports against official information from the Polish authorities," Olszewski urged.

Background:

Overnight on 21-22 November, Lithuanian Foreign Minister Kęstutis Budrys said that Vilnius "categorically rejects false claims circulating on social media" regarding Lithuanian involvement in a drone attack on targets in Kaliningrad Oblast and had not granted permission for the use of its airspace for raids on facilities in Russia.

According to the Telegram channel Exilenova+, activity by Russian air defence systems has been recorded in Baltiysk, Kaliningrad Oblast. The channel's authors suggest that the target of the attack was Baltiysk's port infrastructure. Early reports indicated that drones were heading in that direction earlier today in the morning – they were spotted over the Gulf of Finland, the channel claims. Local residents reported explosions in the port area.

On Saturday 21 November, the Finnish defence forces detected a drone attack on a Russian merchant vessel west of Suursaari in international waters in the eastern Gulf of Finland.

A Ukrainian expert said the drone had struck the Sparta II, which Russia has used for military operations – specifically to transport weapons from Syria for likely use in the war against Ukraine.

articles.title: Three killed and twelve injured in Russian attack on Kyiv Oblast – photo, videos
articles.summary:
Two people have been killed, another eight injured and a shop building has been damaged as a result of a Russian attack on Vyshneve in the Bucha district of Kyiv Oblast. In the Bila Tserkva district, one person has been killed and four people injured.

Source: Kyiv Oblast Military Administration (KOMA); Tymur Tkachenko, Head of Kyiv Oblast Military Administration; social media

Details: KOMA initially reported that a shop building had been damaged in the Bucha district and a man had been injured.

Social media reports indicate that a Novus supermarket in Vyshneve sustained damage.

Tkachenko later reported that one person had been killed and three others injured in Vyshneve as a result of the attack. One of those injured is in a serious condition.

Quote from Tkachenko: "People had simply gone to the shop to buy groceries. An ordinary shopping trip turned into a tragedy because of a Russian attack."

Details: The fire in the shop building has been extinguished.

Tkachenko later reported that the death toll from the strike on Vyshneve had risen to two and the number of people injured had risen to eight.

Meanwhile, one person was killed and four others injured in the Bila Tserkva district as a result of the Russian attack.

Quote from Tkachenko: "Sadly, the enemy has killed another person in the Bila Tserkva district. A fire broke out in a house as a result of the enemy attack. A man was killed. Rescue workers recovered his body from beneath the rubble.

Four more people were injured. One woman was rescued from a damaged house and hospitalised with a head injury and concussion. Another woman was injured by the blast wave. In the city of Bila Tserkva, two people were injured when debris from an enemy drone fell near a shop. Both were taken to hospital.

A house, two cars and premises belonging to a business were also damaged."

articles.title: UK right-wingers distance themselves from Trump: Putin is not our friend
articles.summary:
The British populist party Reform UK and the Conservatives have distanced themselves from US President Donald Trump after he posted a photo of himself with Russian ruler Vladimir Putin captioned "my friend".

Source: The Guardian, as reported by European Pravda

Details: Asked for his reaction, Richard Tice, deputy leader of Reform UK – the British party most closely associated with Trump – replied: "Horror".

Quote from Tice: "It's just wrong at every level … And it's a grave mistake. He is not our friend, Putin. He is, as others have said, a murderous dictator. And no one is in any doubt about that."

Details: Asked whether Nigel Farage, leader of Reform UK and a friend of Trump, would discuss this with the US president, Tice replied: "Oh, there have been a number of occasions where one could agree with Trump, and then disagree with him. There have been more occasions recently when clearly we have disagreed with him and said so very explicitly. And in a sense, that's the nature of long friendships. Sometimes you'll agree and sometimes you'll disagree. And, I think the disagreements are growing."

Reform UK and the Conservative party under the leadership of Kemi Badenoch, both of whom welcomed Trump's re-election in 2024, are increasingly seeking to distance themselves from the US president amid doubts over his temperament and judgement, while his attacks on Iran have led to rising global energy prices.

Asked about the "my friend" post, Alex Burghart, Badenoch's deputy, replied that he was "very sad" about it.

Quote from Burghart: "I'm sad and I'm depressed, because the world that I grew up in was one in which the United States was a defender of freedom. I worry that we might be moving into a world where that isn't the case any more."

Details: Asked about his party's previous support for Trump, Burghart replied: "If you look at what the Conservative party is proposing in terms of defence and foreign policy, it's very clear that we are still on the side of freedom, and we're the party that has said that we will put up defence spending to what NATO wants it to be."

Background:

Trump previously posted a series of photographs on Truth Social from his recent visit to China. One of them shows the American president together with Putin. The photograph is captioned "my friend".

Trump also called Putin his friend when he met him on Thursday on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Shenzhen, China.

articles.title: Ukrainian forces down jet-powered drone with a Kalashnikov rifle – video
articles.summary:
The Ukrainian military personnel have posted footage showing how they brought down a Russian jet-powered drone using a Kalashnikov assault rifle.

Source: 81st Separate Slobozhanske Airmobile Brigade

Details: The drone was shot down on the Sloviansk front in Donetsk Oblast. Troops from a mobile fire group belonging to the brigade's anti-aircraft missile battalion brought it down with a folding-stock Kalashnikov while on combat duty.

Quote from one of the soldiers: "I shot it down! I shot it down with a rifle, I did!"

https://www.facebook.com/plugins/video.php?href=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.facebook.com%2Freel%2F1855640182133227%2F&show_text=0&width=243

Details: The unit did not specify the type of Russian military jet-powered drone that the troops shot down.

Quote from a brigade spokesperson: "No matter how fast their drones fly, our troops will shoot them down. With all means available to us. Because this is our sky."

For reference: The folding-stock Kalashnikov assault rifle was developed for use in confined spaces. The weapon uses 5.45mm calibre ammunition and has a stated rate of fire of 600 rounds per minute.

Background: Ukraine's General Staff previously reported that during October 2026, Ukraine's defence forces brought down 4,859 out of the 6,473 Shahed-type strike drones that Russia had used for attacks on Ukraine.

articles.title: Russians strike gas service facility and two petrol stations, injuring people
articles.summary:
Russian forces have struck a gas service facility in Dnipropetrovsk Oblast with an aerial bomb and attacked two petrol stations belonging to Ukrnafta, Ukraine's largest oil and gas producer, in Zaporizhzhia Oblast.

Source: press service for Naftogaz Group, Ukraine's national oil and gas company

Details: A Naftogaz employee, who is currently in hospital, was injured in the attack in Dnipropetrovsk Oblast. Two more of his colleagues are suffering from concussion. All of those injured are receiving the necessary medical treatment.

Quote from Serhii Fedorenko, Acting Chairman of the Board of Naftogaz Group: "Russia is deliberately targeting the people who provide gas and heat to frontline communities every day. Our people are working under constant danger. They continue to do their jobs, because warmth in people's homes depends on them."

Details: Naftogaz notes that over the past two days, Russia has been actively attacking its gas workers, service vehicles and gas infrastructure facilities.

Background: Since the start of 2026, the Russians have attacked Naftogaz facilities more than 250 times.

articles.title: Teenager killed by Russian drone explosion in Sumy Oblast
articles.summary:
Kyrylo Kozburh, a 15-year-old from the village of Mazivka, has been killed as a result of the explosion of a Russian drone in the Novoslobidska hromada in Sumy Oblast. [A hromada is an administrative unit designating a village, several villages, or a town, and their adjacent territories.]

Source: Oleh Hryhorov, Head of Sumy Oblast Military Administration; Olha Harkavenko, Head of Novoslobidska hromada

Quote from Hryhorov: "Sadly, a 14-year-old boy died today in Sumy Oblast as a result of an enemy drone explosion.

The tragedy occurred this morning in the Novoslobidska hromada.

Early reports indicate that two local residents came across an enemy unmanned aerial vehicle, which detonated. The teenager died at the scene from the severe injuries he sustained."

Details: Harkavenko confirmed that 15-year-old Kyrylo, a resident of the village of Mazivka, was killed as a result of the detonation of an FPV-type unmanned aerial vehicle.

articles.title: Slovak foreign minister hints Ukrainians were behind the invasion of Czechoslovakia
articles.summary:
Slovak Foreign Minister Juraj Blanár has suggested that Ukrainians were behind the Soviet occupation of Czechoslovakia in 1968.

Source: Slovak newspaper Denník N; European Pravda

Details: Blanár claimed that the first Soviet regiment to arrive in Slovakia was Ukrainian, and that "Brezhnev was Ukrainian".

"You can't be serious," responded Michal Šimečka of the opposition Progressive Slovakia party, pointing out that the USSR was a prison of nations, including the Ukrainian people, and that the Politburo, which made the decision to invade Czechoslovakia, was based in Moscow.

Blanár said that there was no symbolic significance whatsoever to the government holding a meeting of the Slovak-Russian Intergovernmental Commission on 17 November. "We held the meeting on a working day which is a public holiday, which we observed as befits such an occasion. It is a holiday that is important to us," Blanár said.

Blanár emphasised that 17 November is also International Students' Day, among other things, recalling that in 1939 Nazi Germany closed all higher education institutions following the funeral of Czech student Jan Opletal.

Support Ukrainska Pravda on Patreon to help us keep reporting!

articles.title: UK government minister says "butcher" Putin is no friend of the United Kingdom
articles.summary:
UK government minister Hamish Falconer has become the latest political figure to condemn US President Donald Trump's comments about the Russian ruler.

Source: Falconer, the UK's Minister of State (Minister for Intergovernmental Relations and European Relations), in an interview with Sky News, as reported by European Pravda

Details: The minister called Putin a "butcher" and condemned "Russia's barbaric, illegal war".

"The cost has been so high and practically no higher for the country that that man represents," he said.

Quote: "Russia is suffering terribly from a war which is illegal. It is brutal. It is starving Russian young people of so many opportunities, as you hear from them directly. So would Vladimir Putin be my friend? No. And he's not a friend to the UK either."

Details: Asked whether the UK government would express its position regarding the comments about "friendship", Falconer added: "The prime minister speaks to the president regularly and is in absolutely no way pulling his punches about the strength of feeling that the UK has as a whole about Russia's invasion of Ukraine."

Background:

Trump previously posted a series of photographs on Truth Social from his recent visit to China. One of them shows the American president together with Putin. The photograph is captioned "my friend".

Trump also called Putin his friend when he met him on Thursday on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Shenzhen, China.

On 20 November, the American president said that the Kremlin leader had assured him that he wanted to end the war with Ukraine diplomatically, and also said that Putin is "having a hard time right now" because of the war he started against Ukraine.

articles.title: Russian attacks cause power outages in five Ukrainian oblasts
articles.summary:
Some consumers in Dnipropetrovsk, Zhytomyr, Rivne, Odesa and Kharkiv oblasts were left without power as of the morning of 22 November due to Russian attacks on a number of energy facilities over the past 24 hours.

Source: Ministry of Energy

Details: The most difficult situation as of this morning is in Odesa Oblast. A significant proportion of consumers there remain without electricity, as Russia continues to attack critical energy facilities, which makes repair work following previous strikes considerably more difficult.

Thanks to the repairs carried out in the morning, it has been possible to begin partially restoring the electricity supply to critical infrastructure facilities in Odesa and the surrounding districts.

The power engineers' top priority remains to ensure the stable operation of those facilities. Backup power supply options and other technical solutions are also being worked out to gradually restore power to the remaining consumers.

The Ministry of Energy emphasises that the damage is extensive, so repairs will take time.

Background:

From 23 to 27 November, schools in Odesa will switch to remote learning due to significant disruptions to heating, electricity and water supplies.

On the morning of 22 November, Ukraine's energy companies reported that the electricity situation in Odesa and surrounding districts remains extremely difficult due to damage to the main power grids.
